title: Retinal Vascular Complications of Dengue Fever, an Unexplored Entity:
abstract: Introduction: Systemic manifestations of dengue fever are well characterised, however ocular involvement has historically been considered a rare and under-recognised complication. Although less common,it can lead to visual impairment or blindness if not promptly addressed. Case Report: We describe a case series of five patients, all with clinically and serologically confirmed dengue fever who developed retinal vascular complications. Demographic data were extracted, along with systemic history (interval between dengue infection diagnosis to the onset of ocular symptoms, and interval between visual complaint to ophthalmic evaluation), and presenting best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA). Pre-existing identifiable causes of retinal vascular occlusion (RVO) , if any, were recorded. All patients underwent fundus photo and spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) examinations. Discussion: Seven eyes of five patients were included, all patients were female with a mean age of 25.8 years (range 19-32 years). None had identifiable pre-existing risk factor for RVO. The mean interval between dengue fever diagnosis to the onset of visual symptoms was 9.6 days (range 7-14 days). Patient one presented with sequential, bilateral central retinal artery occlusion; patient two came in with bilateral Purtscher-like retinopathy. Another patients exhibit paracentral acute-middle maculopathy (PAMM), and branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO). Presenting BCVA ranged widely from 20/20 with paracentral scotoma to 20/800, reflecting the heterogenous severity of the vascular insult across the cohort. Conclusion: Dengue fever can produce a diverse spectrum of retinal vascular complications, typically manifesting one to three weeks after the onset of systemic illness. Spectral-domain OCT is central to the diagnosis, even when clinical examination is unremarkable. Prompt recognition and management is needed to avoid ocular complications and visual impairment. Keywords: dengue fever, dengue eye disease, retinal vascular occlusion, macular edema

Case Report: We describe a case series of five patients, all with clinically and serologically confirmed dengue fever who developed retinal vascular complications. Demographic data were extracted, along with systemic history (interval between dengue infection diagnosis to the onset of ocular symptoms, and interval between visual complaint to ophthalmic evaluation), and presenting best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA). Pre-existing identifiable causes of retinal vascular occlusion (RVO) , if any, were recorded. All patients underwent fundus photo and spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) examinations. Discussion: Seven eyes of five patients were included, all patients were female with a mean age of 25.8 years (range 19-32 years). None had identifiable pre-existing risk factor for RVO. The mean interval between dengue fever diagnosis to the onset of visual symptoms was 9.6 days (range 7-14 days). Patient one presented with sequential, bilateral central retinal artery occlusion; patient two came in with bilateral Purtscher-like retinopathy. Another patients exhibit paracentral acute-middle maculopathy (PAMM), and branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO). Presenting BCVA ranged widely from 20/20 with paracentral scotoma to 20/800, reflecting the heterogenous severity of the vascular insult across the cohort. Conclusion: Dengue fever can produce a diverse spectrum of retinal vascular complications, typically manifesting one to three weeks after the onset of systemic illness. Spectral-domain OCT is central to the diagnosis, even when clinical examination is unremarkable. Prompt recognition and management is needed to avoid ocular complications and visual impairment. Keywords: dengue fever, dengue eye disease, retinal vascular occlusion, macular edema

analysis.summary_en: This case report explores the under-recognised retinal vascular complications of dengue fever, highlighting a diverse spectrum of ocular manifestations typically occurring one to three weeks after systemic illness onset. Five patients with confirmed dengue fever developed retinal vascular issues, including central retinal artery occlusion, Purtscher-like retinopathy, paracentral acute-middle maculopathy (PAMM), and branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO). The mean interval between dengue diagnosis and visual symptoms was 9.6 days. Spectral-domain OCT is emphasized as a critical diagnostic tool, even when clinical findings are inconspicuous. The study underscores the importance of early detection and management to prevent visual impairment. However, the evidence is limited to a single case series, which may not fully represent the broader population or long-term outcomes.

abstract_zh: 引言:登革热的系统表现已被充分描述,但眼部受累历来被认为是一种罕见且未被充分认识的并发症。尽管较为少见,但若不及时处理,可能导致视力损害或失明。病例报告:我们描述了五例患者的病例系列,这些患者均经临床和血清学确诊为登革热,并出现了视网膜血管并发症。收集了人口统计数据、系统病史(从登革病毒感染诊断到眼部症状发作的时间间隔,以及从视力问题出现到眼科评估的时间间隔),以及初始最佳矫正视力(BCVA)。记录了所有患者是否存在已知的视网膜血管阻塞(RVO)的可识别原因。所有患者均接受了眼底照相和光谱域光学相干断层扫描(SD-OCT)检查。讨论:纳入了五名患者的七只眼睛,所有患者均为女性,平均年龄为25.8岁(年龄范围19-32岁)。无患者存在可识别的RVO风险因素。从登革热感染诊断到视力症状发作的平均时间间隔为9.6天(范围7-14天)。患者一表现为双侧中央动脉阻塞;患者二在就诊时出现双侧Purtscher样视网膜病变。其他患者则表现出旁中心性急性中期黄斑病变(PAMM)和分支视网膜静脉阻塞(BRVO)。初始BCVA范围广泛,从伴有旁中心暗点的20/20到20/800,反映了队列研究中血管损伤的异质性严重程度。结论:登革热可导致多种视网膜血管并发症,通常在系统性疾病发作后1至3周出现。即使临床检查无明显异常,光谱域OCT在诊断诊断中也至关重要。及时识别和管理是避免眼部并发症和视力损害的关键。关键词:登革热,登革热眼病,视网膜血管阻塞,黄斑水肿

title: Meteorological predictors of dengue hemorrhagic fever incidence in Cilacap Regency, Indonesia: A time series analysis
abstract: Objective: To analyze the nonlinear relationship between meteorological predictors and dengue hemorrhagic fever, and to quantify the meteorologically attributable fraction of dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) during 2021-2025 in Cilacap Regency. Methods: This ecological time series design used sequential three-stage analytical tools, including a cross-correlation function (CCF) analysis applied to identify lag structures, Granger causality within a vector autoregression (VAR) framework used to confirm directional temporal precedence, and a quasi-Poisson Distributed Lag Nonlinear Model (DLNM) with natural cubic spline crossbases over a 28-day lag window used to estimate the exposure-response relationship. Autoregressive terms alongside long-term trends and seasonal splines were incorporated to account for autocorrelation and potential confounding. Results: Granger causality testing confirmed unidirectional of DHF relationships across all four predictors, including mean temperature, rainfall, relative humidity, and wind speed (all P <0.05). Among these, daily rainfall emerged as the dominant predictor [relative risk ( RR ) 4.23; 95% CI 2.10-8.52)], a peak CCF lag of 7 days, and an attributable fraction of 27.58%. The mean temperature displayed a J-shaped exposure-response curve, with a protective nadir at 26.5°C, and markedly elevated risk above 28 °C [ RR 2.13; 95% CI 1.43-3.19; Attributable Fraction (AF) = 6.22%]. Relative humidity (AF= -14.40%) and wind speed (AF= -3.37%) demonstrated complex nonlinear patterns contributing net protective attributable fractions. Overall, the model explained 52.26% of the null deviance (QAIC= 3 984.23). Conclusions: Rainfall and temperature were the meteorological predictors most strongly associated with DHF incidence in Cilacap Regency. This finding provides evidence for actionable vector control program and early warning system of DHF to consider the utilization of meteorological predictor to prevent DHF outbreak in Cilacap.
journal: Asian Pacific Journal of Tropical Medicine

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在分析气象预测因子与登革出血热(DHF)发病率 之间的非线性关系,并量化 2021-2025 年期间印度尼西亚 cilacap 县 DHF 的气象归因分数。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究采用生态时间序列设计,分析了 2021 年至 2025 年期间印度尼西亚 cilacap 县的数据。研究包括连续的三阶段分析工具,以评估 DHF 与气象预测因子之间的关系。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究采用交叉相关函数(CCF)分析以识别滞后结构,使用 媒介 自回归(VAR)框架内的格兰杰因果关系检验以确认时间顺序的单向性,并采用准泊松分布滞后非线性模型(DLNM)以估计暴露-反应关系,该模型在 28 天的滞后窗口内使用自然三次样条交叉基底。
elements_zh.main_results: 格兰杰因果关系检验确认了 DHF 与所有四个预测因子之间的单向关系,包括平均温度、降雨量、相对湿度和风速(所有 P < 0.05)。每日降雨量是主要预测因子,其相对风险(RR)为 4.23(95% CI 2.10-8.52),归因分数为 27.58%。平均温度表现出 J 型暴露-反应曲线,其保护性最低点为 26.5°C,且在高于 28°C 时风险显著升高(RR 2.13;95% CI 1.43-3.19;AF = 6.22%)。相对湿度(AF = -14.40%)和风速(AF = -3.37%)表现出复杂的非线性模式,贡献了净保护性归因分数。总体而言,该模型解释了 52.26% 的零偏差(QAIC = 3984.23)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究发现,降雨量和温度是与 cilacap 县 DHF 发病率 最强相关的气象预测因子,突显了这些因素与 DHF 之间的非线性关系。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,将气象预测因子纳入 媒介 控制计划和早期预警系统,有助于预防 cilacap 县 DHF 暴发。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 研究中纳入了自回归项和长期趋势,以考虑自相关性和潜在的混杂因素,但研究的生态设计可能限制了推断个体层面因果关系的能力。证据强度中等,因为其基于摘要分析。

source_body_en: Objective: To analyze the nonlinear relationship between meteorological predictors and dengue hemorrhagic fever, and to quantify the meteorologically attributable fraction of dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) during 2021-2025 in Cilacap Regency. Methods: This ecological time series design used sequential three-stage analytical tools, including a cross-correlation function (CCF) analysis applied to identify lag structures, Granger causality within a vector autoregression (VAR) framework used to confirm directional temporal precedence, and a quasi-Poisson Distributed Lag Nonlinear Model (DLNM) with natural cubic spline crossbases over a 28-day lag window used to estimate the exposure-response relationship. Autoregressive terms alongside long-term trends and seasonal splines were incorporated to account for autocorrelation and potential confounding. Results: Granger causality testing confirmed unidirectional of DHF relationships across all four predictors, including mean temperature, rainfall, relative humidity, and wind speed (all P <0.05). Among these, daily rainfall emerged as the dominant predictor [relative risk ( RR ) 4.23; 95% CI 2.10-8.52)], a peak CCF lag of 7 days, and an attributable fraction of 27.58%. The mean temperature displayed a J-shaped exposure-response curve, with a protective nadir at 26.5°C, and markedly elevated risk above 28 °C [ RR 2.13; 95% CI 1.43-3.19; Attributable Fraction (AF) = 6.22%]. Relative humidity (AF= -14.40%) and wind speed (AF= -3.37%) demonstrated complex nonlinear patterns contributing net protective attributable fractions. Overall, the model explained 52.26% of the null deviance (QAIC= 3 984.23). Conclusions: Rainfall and temperature were the meteorological predictors most strongly associated with DHF incidence in Cilacap Regency. This finding provides evidence for actionable vector control program and early warning system of DHF to consider the utilization of meteorological predictor to prevent DHF outbreak in Cilacap.
abstract_zh: 目标:分析气象预测因子与登革出血热(DHF)之间的非线性关系,并量化 2021-2025 年期间 cilacap 县 DHF 的气象归因分数。方法:本研究采用生态时间序列设计,使用连续的三阶段分析工具,包括用于识别滞后结构的交叉相关函数(CCF)分析,以及在 媒介 自回归(VAR)框架内使用的格兰杰因果关系检验,以确认时间顺序的单向性。此外,还使用了准泊松分布滞后非线性模型(DLNM),该模型在 28 天的滞后窗口内采用自然三次样条交叉基底,以估计暴露-反应关系。模型中纳入了自回归项、长期趋势和季节性样条,以考虑自相关性和潜在的混杂因素。结果:格兰杰因果关系检验确认了 DHF 与所有四个预测因子之间的单向关系,包括平均温度、降雨量、相对湿度和风速(所有 P < 0.05)。其中,每日降雨量是主要预测因子,其相对风险(RR)为 4.23(95% CI 2.10-8.52),滞后峰值为 7 天,归因分数为 27.58%。平均温度表现出 J 型暴露-反应曲线,其保护性最低点为 26.5°C,且在高于 28°C 时风险显著升高(RR 2.13;95% CI 1.43-3.19;归因分数(AF)= 6.22%)。相对湿度(AF = -14.40%)和风速(AF = -3.37%)表现出复杂的非线性模式,贡献了净保护性归因分数。总体而言,该模型解释了 52.26% 的零偏差(QAIC = 3984.23)。结论:降雨量和温度是与 cilacap 县 DHF 发病率 最强相关的气象预测因子。这一发现为在 DHF 控制计划和早期预警系统中考虑利用气象预测因子以预防 cilacap 县 DHF 暴发 提供了依据。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在分析气象预测因子与登革出血热(DHF)发病率 之间的非线性关系,并量化 2021-2025 年期间印度尼西亚 cilacap 县 DHF 的气象归因分数。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究采用生态时间序列设计,分析了 2021 年至 2025 年期间印度尼西亚 cilacap 县的数据。研究包括连续的三阶段分析工具,以评估 DHF 与气象预测因子之间的关系。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究采用交叉相关函数(CCF)分析以识别滞后结构,使用 媒介 自回归(VAR)框架内的格兰杰因果关系检验以确认时间顺序的单向性,并采用准泊松分布滞后非线性模型(DLNM)以估计暴露-反应关系,该模型在 28 天的滞后窗口内使用自然三次样条交叉基底。
analysis_zh.main_results: 格兰杰因果关系检验确认了 DHF 与所有四个预测因子之间的单向关系,包括平均温度、降雨量、相对湿度和风速(所有 P < 0.05)。每日降雨量是主要预测因子,其相对风险(RR)为 4.23(95% CI 2.10-8.52),归因分数为 27.58%。平均温度表现出 J 型暴露-反应曲线,其保护性最低点为 26.5°C,且在高于 28°C 时风险显著升高(RR 2.13;95% CI 1.43-3.19;AF = 6.22%)。相对湿度(AF = -14.40%)和风速(AF = -3.37%)表现出复杂的非线性模式,贡献了净保护性归因分数。总体而言,该模型解释了 52.26% 的零偏差(QAIC = 3984.23)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究发现,降雨量和温度是与 cilacap 县 DHF 发病率 最强相关的气象预测因子,突显了这些因素与 DHF 之间的非线性关系。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,将气象预测因子纳入 媒介 控制计划和早期预警系统,有助于预防 cilacap 县 DHF 暴发。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 研究中纳入了自回归项和长期趋势,以考虑自相关性和潜在的混杂因素,但研究的生态设计可能限制了推断个体层面因果关系的能力。证据强度中等,因为其基于摘要分析。

title: Expanded Dengue Syndrome With Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome
abstract: Dengue virus infection can present with a wide spectrum of clinical manifestations, ranging from mild febrile illness to severe disease with multiorgan involvement. Neurological complications, though less common, are increasingly recognized in severe dengue, with posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) being a rare association. We report the case of a 16-year-old male presenting with high-grade fever, altered sensorium, and in-hospital seizures in the setting of dengue virus infection. Laboratory evaluation showed dengue NS1 antigen and IgM antibody positivity, thrombocytopenia, and deranged liver and renal function tests. Initial MRI brain was normal, but a repeat MRI following seizure episodes revealed PRES. Supportive management, including adequate hydration, antibiotics, antiepileptic, diuretics, and ventilatory support, led to full neurological recovery. This case illustrates a rare presentation of dengue-associated PRES with multiorgan involvement, highlighting the importance of early recognition and timely supportive management.

title: Persistent dengue NS1 antigen in a patient with visceral leishmaniasis: A diagnostic and therapeutic odyssey
abstract: Visceral leishmaniasis (VL) and dengue are both life-threatening vector-borne diseases and are endemic in many low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Despite being caused by different pathogens and transmitted by distinct vectors, Leishmania parasite-dengue virus (DENV) coinfection can complicate the course of diseases, their diagnoses and their treatments due to their some similar clinical features. This study presents a 23-year-old male patient from the Dang district of Nepal, a migrant worker in Malaysia who experienced a prolonged intermittent fever. The patient’s symptoms, clinical diagnosis and disease management approach across three different countries (Malaysia, India, and Nepal) were recorded. The patient was initially diagnosed positive for dengue in Malaysia during his immigration period as a worker. Due to a persistent fever, he had to return to Nepal. In India, other investigations erroneously suspected hematological malignancy. Finally, after a third febrile episode, VL was correctly diagnosed, but initial treatment with Liposomal Amphotericin B (LAMB) failed, resulting in relapse. During this period, the dengue NS1 antigen remained positive. Despite treatment with six doses of LAMB, the patient showed no adequate response. After negative test results for dengue NS1 antigen, IgM, and IgG antibody, a highly effective rescue intervention of miltefosine led to the resolution of VL. This study underscores the challenges and complexities of diagnosis associated with Leishmania -DENV coinfection. These concomitant infections appear to be the cause of the prolonged persistence of dengue fever, and progression from an asymptomatic Leishmania infection to a symptomatic VL. It also highlights the need for diagnostic tools and effective management strategies to address coinfections.

title: Unraveling stress levels in post-dengue adults in a low-middle-income country.
abstract: BACKGROUND OBJECTIVES: Psychological well-being among dengue patients has often been rather unnoticed, despite evidence showing a notable proportion experiencing psychological distress during the illness and the post-infectious period. This study aimed to assess the prevalence and associated factors of stress one month after hospital discharge among adults with dengue fever in Colombo District, Sri Lanka. METHODS: A longitudinal study was conducted in 2019 among 480 patients discharged after dengue treatment. Participants were selected using systematic sampling and followed up for one month after fever onset. Prevalence of stress was assessed using the validated Depression, Anxiety and Stress -21. Selected correlates were assessed using a pre-tested interviewer-administered questionnaire. Binomial multiple logistic regression was used for analysis. RESULTS: Of the 480 participants, 406 responded (response rate: 84.58). The majority were males (n=244, 60.15%) and aged 18-35 years (n=281, 69.2%). The prevalence of stress at one month post-infection was 7.9% (95% CI: 5.5-10.9). Significant correlates of stress included female gender (AOR=3.24; 95% CI: 1.45-7.26), presence of headache (AOR=3.26; 95% CI: 1.39-7.61), and myalgia (AOR=4.16; 95% CI: 1.74-9.92) during the post-infection period. INTERPRETATION CONCLUSION: Approximately one in twelve adults experienced stress one month after dengue infection. Post-infection symptoms such as headache and myalgia were significant predictors of stress. These findings highlight the need for routine psychological screening and targeted interventions during follow-up care for dengue patients.

title: Septic shock mimicking dengue and typhoid: A case report
abstract: Rationale: In dengue- and typhoid-endemic regions, a reactive IgM often anchors the diagnosis, yet severe sepsis can drive polyclonal B-cell activation and low-specificity antibodies that yield false-positive results. Patient concerns: A 57-year-old previously healthy male patient presented with six days of fever, crampy abdominal pain, and mucoid diarrhea, followed by progressive weakness and circulatory collapse. Diagnosis: Septic shock with multiple organ dysfunction (SOFA 10), thrombocytopenia, markedly raised procalcitonin, acute kidney injury, conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, and pancreatic edema. Dengue IgM was positive and Salmonella TUBEX was borderline positive, but both reverted to negative on repeat testing. The final diagnosis was culture-negative septic shock of presumed gastrointestinal origin with secondary acute pancreatitis. Interventions: Fluid resuscitation, norepinephrine and vasopressin, empirical ceftriaxone, nutritional support, and conservative pancreatitis care. Outcomes: Cultures obtained after antibiotics were sterile; procalcitonin fell from 7.95 to 0.15 ng/mL by day 7, and the patient recovered and was discharged on day 13. Lessons: In septic shock, an isolated reactive IgM should be interpreted cautiously and integrated with biomarker trends, cultures, and organ-dysfunction patterns.
journal: Asian Pacific Journal of Tropical Medicine

title: Epidemiological Determinants of Dengue Infection in Dhaka:A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Background: In Dhaka, Bangladesh, dengue outbreaks are influenced by demographic, geographic, and housingfactors, which presents valuable insights for improving preventive measures and reducing public health hazards.Objectives: The main objective of this study was to identify the prevalence of dengue infection in Dhaka and thefactors that contribute to it.Study designs: This study used secondary data from a publicly available Kaggle dataset and included 1,000respondents.Methods: To examine relationships between dengue positivity and contributing factors, chi-square tests wereconducted using SPSS version 26.Results: The study found that 53.3% of participants had dengue, with 52.7% of cases occurring in females and47.3% in males.

source_records.abstract: Background: In Dhaka, Bangladesh, dengue outbreaks are influenced by demographic, geographic, and housingfactors, which presents valuable insights for improving preventive measures and reducing public health hazards.Objectives: The main objective of this study was to identify the prevalence of dengue infection in Dhaka and thefactors that contribute to it.Study designs: This study used secondary data from a publicly available Kaggle dataset and included 1,000respondents.Methods: To examine relationships between dengue positivity and contributing factors, chi-square tests wereconducted using SPSS version 26.Results: The study found that 53.3% of participants had dengue, with 52.7% of cases occurring in females and47.3% in males.

title: Chronic Complications Following Dengue Infection: A Scoping Review
abstract: Dengue virus infection has increased substantially in Latin America, prompting epidemiological alerts from regional health authorities in recent years. While most published research focuses on the acute phase, chronic multisystemic sequelae remain poorly characterized. This scoping review aimed to identify and describe chronic complications in adult patients following dengue infection, as reported in the available scientific literature. A scoping review was conducted following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. A structured Population, Concept, Context (PCC) question guided searches of PubMed (National Library of Medicine, Bethesda, Maryland), Scopus (Elsevier, Amsterdam, the Netherlands), Google Scholar (Google, Mountain View, California), EMBASE (Elsevier, Amsterdam, the Netherlands), Cochrane Library (John Wiley & Sons, Hoboken, New Jersey), and LILACS (BIREME, São Paulo, Brazil), and gray literature from January 2005 to June 15, 2026. Articles were screened independently by eight reviewers using Rayyan; inter-rater reliability was assessed using Fleiss' kappa (κ = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.74-0.88), and disagreements were resolved by consensus. Of the 222 identified records, 62 studies met the inclusion criteria after deduplication and full-text screening. Neurological complications were the most frequently represented category among the included publications (30.6%, n = 19), followed by ophthalmological (19.4%, n = 12), heterogeneous persistent symptoms (12.9%, n = 8), fatigue (9.7%, n = 6), multisystemic (9.7%, n = 6), psychiatric (9.7%, n = 6), cardiological (4.8%, n = 3), and immunological (3.2%, n = 2) complications. These proportions reflect the distribution of the published literature rather than the clinical prevalence of complications among dengue patients, given that approximately one-third of the included studies were case reports or case series. The evidence base includes the largest population-based cohort of post-acute dengue sequelae to date (n = 55,870, Singapore), a two-year disability-adjusted life-year (DALY) burden analysis from the same registry, the first systematic review of dengue-associated Guillain-Barré syndrome, the first reported case of chronic dengue encephalitis with brain-tissue DENV RNA confirmed by metagenomic sequencing, and two narrative reviews that substantially expanded the evidence base on psychiatric sequelae. Dengue infection is associated with a broad and heterogeneous spectrum of chronic complications affecting multiple organ systems, including elevated post-acute cardiovascular, neuropsychiatric, and autoimmune risks, as well as a measurable disease and healthcare cost burden. The absence of a consistent relationship between acute severity and chronic outcomes supports structured, evidence-based, long-term post-dengue follow-up, particularly for patients with persistent symptoms or clinically relevant risk factors and for underrepresented Latin American populations.

media_mentions.content: Abstract Dengue virus infection has increased substantially in Latin America, prompting epidemiological alerts from regional health authorities in recent years. Dengue infection is associated with a broad and heterogeneous spectrum of chronic complications affecting multiple organ systems, including elevated post-acute cardiovascular, neuropsychiatric, and autoimmune risks, as well as a measurable disease and healthcare cost burden. The absence of a consistent relationship between acute severity and chronic outcomes supports structured, evidence-based, long-term post-dengue follow-up, particularly for patients with persistent symptoms or clinically relevant risk factors and for underrepresented Latin American populations. Introduction & Background Dengue virus (DENV) is a positive-sense single-stranded RNA flavivirus transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti and, to a lesser extent, Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. It comprises four antigenically distinct serotypes (DENV-1 through DENV-4), each capable of causing clinically indistinguishable illness. However, infection with one serotype confers only serotype-specific long-term immunity. The World Health Organization estimates that approximately 100-400 million dengue infections occur annually, with roughly 40% of the world's population currently at risk; the number of notified cases increased tenfold between 2000 and 2019, from approximately 500,000 to over 5.2 million across more than 80 countries [1]. Clinically, dengue infection is classified into three sequential phases: the febrile phase (days 1-7), characterized by sudden-onset high fever and myalgia; the critical phase (days 3-7), defined by plasma leakage and thrombocytopenia; and the recovery phase (days 7-10), during which reabsorption of extravasated fluids occurs. Disease severity spans a spectrum from dengue without warning signs to dengue with warning signs and severe dengue, the latter encompassing dengue hemorrhagic fever and dengue shock syndrome [1]. This well-characterized acute presentation has shaped the dominant clinical and research focus on short-term management and the reduction of case fatality. Despite the extensive literature on acute dengue, the chronic multisystemic sequelae that emerge or persist beyond the recovery phase remain comparatively understudied [2]. No universally accepted definition or classification framework exists for subacute or chronic complications following dengue infection. For this review, chronic complications were operationally defined as clinical manifestations, symptoms, or sequelae that persisted or emerged more than four weeks after the onset of dengue symptoms. The four-week threshold was selected because it substantially exceeds the typical duration of the acute and recovery phases of dengue infection (up to approximately 10 days), providing a conservative, clinically distinguishable cutoff between expected acute-phase resolution and true chronic persistence, consistent with thresholds used elsewhere in the post-infectious and post-viral syndrome literature. This threshold was selected to distinguish persistent or late manifestations from complications confined to the expected acute and early recovery phases. Because certain neurological and cardiovascular conditions, including Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) and cardiomyopathies, may begin during the acute or early post-acute period but result in persistent disability or long-term sequelae, these conditions were eligible when persistent manifestations beyond the four-week threshold were documented [3,4]. This operational definition therefore encompasses two distinct but overlapping constructs: (i) post-acute persistent or new-onset symptoms with a delayed or gradual course (e.g., post-dengue fatigue, persistent arthralgia), and (ii) long-term sequelae resulting from irreversible tissue damage sustained during the acute phase (e.g., residual neurological deficits after stroke or peripheral nerve injury) when disability persisted beyond four weeks. Both categories were included under the umbrella of "chronic complications" for the purposes of this review. The pathophysiological mechanisms proposed to contribute to post-dengue chronicity are multifactorial, involving direct viral neurotropism, immune-mediated mechanisms such as molecular mimicry and autoantibody production, persistent cytokine dysregulation, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis disruption, and autonomic nervous system dysregulation [5,6]. However, the relative contribution of each mechanism to specific chronic complications and the extent to which these pathways are supported by direct clinical or laboratory evidence remain unclear. This scoping review aims to systematically map and describe the chronic complications reported following dengue infection in adults across organ systems, characterize their underlying evidence base and proposed pathophysiological mechanisms, and identify gaps in the literature (particularly the scarcity of prospective, population-level, and Latin American data) to inform future research and post-dengue clinical follow-up. Review Methods Study Design We conducted a scoping review following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) framework. The guiding research question was, what chronic complications have been reported following dengue infection in adult patients, and what is their frequency, onset, duration, and underlying evidence base across organ systems and geographic regions? This question was structured using the PCC framework: Population (adult patients with prior dengue infection confirmed by serology or PCR), Concept (chronic complications across cardiovascular, immunological, neurological, ophthalmological, psychiatric, and multisystemic domains), and Context (adult populations recovering from dengue infection worldwide, as reported in the international scientific literature). The review protocol was registered with the Open Science Framework (OSF; osf.io/7dvuj, Center for Open Science, Charlottesville, Virginia) on May 30, 2026. Database searches had commenced before registration; therefore, the registration was retrospective relative to the initiation of the search process. This timing is reported transparently as a methodological limitation. Search Strategy A structured search covering January 2005 to June 15, 2026, was conducted across PubMed (National Library of Medicine, Bethesda, Maryland), Google Scholar (Google, Mountain View, California), Scopus (Elsevier, Amsterdam, the Netherlands), EMBASE (Elsevier, Amsterdam, the Netherlands), Cochrane Library (John Wiley & Sons, Hoboken, New Jersey), LILACS (BIREME, São Paulo, Brazil), and gray literature sources. Gray literature was manually searched through institutional repositories and websites of tropical medicine societies and universities in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Mexico, and Peru to capture regionally relevant Latin American findings not indexed in the major databases above (complete search strategies by database, including gray literature, are detailed in Appendices). The search terms included "dengue," "dengue fever," "post-infection," "chronic," "long term," "complications," "sequelae," and "acute," combined using the Boolean operators AND, OR, and NOT. Filters were applied for language and study population (human adults). Full-text articles were retrieved from open-access repositories and through institutional subscriptions. Complete search strings and database yields are provided in Appendices. Eligibility Criteria Inclusion criteria: (1) adult population (≥18 years); (2) serologically or PCR-confirmed dengue diagnosis; (3) chronic complications, defined as those appearing after four weeks post-infection or following a natural course exceeding one month (with the exceptions noted above for GBS and cardiomyopathies). Exclusion criteria: (1) articles published before 2005; (2) exclusively pediatric populations; (3) descriptions limited to acute-phase complications resolving within four weeks; (4) absence of serological/PCR confirmation; (5) and inaccessible full text. Study Selection and Inter-rater Reliability Identified records were imported into Rayyan for duplicate removal and eligibility screening. Eight independent reviewers screened titles and abstracts, followed by full-text assessment of potentially eligible articles. Blind mode in Rayyan was strictly maintained during title- and abstract-level screening by all eight reviewers to prevent selection bias and was unblinded only after initial decisions were logged for consensus resolution. Inter-rater reliability was formally assessed using Fleiss' kappa coefficient, which was appropriate given the involvement of eight independent reviewers in the screening. The kappa value obtained was κ = 0.81 (95% CI: 0.74-0.88), indicating strong agreement among reviewers. Disagreements were resolved by consensus. Data Extraction and Quality Assessment Data extraction and Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) quality appraisal were performed independently by pairs of reviewers (four pairs drawn from the same eight-reviewer screening team), each assigned a subset of the 62 included studies; disagreements were first resolved through discussion within each pair and, when unresolved, adjudicated by the senior/supervising author. A standardized extraction matrix was used to record the authors, publication year, country, study design, study objectives, DOI/link, and primary complication category. For the purposes of this review, an included "study" was defined as an eligible publication or report that met the predefined inclusion criteria, regardless of study design. Each included study was assigned a primary complication category based on the principal chronic outcome investigated. When a study reported outcomes involving multiple organ systems, it was assigned to the category corresponding to its primary outcome or predominant complication domain. Studies addressing multiple organ systems without a predominant domain were classified as multisystemic. The methodological quality of all 62 included studies was assessed using the JBI critical appraisal checklists appropriate to each study design and is summarized in Table 1 (main text). Design-specific JBI checklists were applied (cohort studies for cohorts; systematic reviews for systematic reviews; case series; case reports; analytical cross-sectional studies for cross-sectional designs; and text and opinion papers for narrative reviews), with quality scored as the percentage of "yes" items met and categorized a priori as high (≥75%), moderate (50-74%), or low (<50%), per conventional JBI thresholds. As each checklist evaluates design-specific domains, these categories reflect within-design rigor rather than a directly comparable cross-design scale. No meta-analysis or pooled statistical synthesis was planned or performed, given the substantial heterogeneity in study designs, populations, outcome definitions, and follow-up durations across included studies; findings are instead synthesized narratively, with counts, percentages, and effect estimates (e.g., relative risks, hazard ratios, and 95% CIs) reported as originally presented by the primary studies. Results Study Selection The search identified 222 raw records; 52 duplicates were removed, leaving 170 unique records for title/abstract screening. Seventeen were excluded at this stage, and 153 reports were sought and assessed at full text. Ninety-one were excluded (53 acute-phase-only, 15 with inaccessible or restricted full text, 12 addressing unrelated topics, and 11 exclusively pediatric), yielding 62 studies included in the final synthesis (Figure 1). Characteristics of Included Studies Of the 62 included studies, the majority were indexed in PubMed, with additional records identified via Google Scholar, Scopus, and EMBASE. Study designs varied, comprising prospective and retrospective cohort studies, including several large population-based cohorts from Singapore, Sudan, and Brazil, systematic and narrative reviews, case series, and case reports. Methodological quality also varied across study designs: 35 studies (56%) were classified as high quality, 21 (34%) as moderate quality, and 6 (10%) as low quality according to the predefined JBI criteria (Table 1). Notably, case reports and case series constituted an important proportion of the evidence base and were interpreted primarily as signals of rare or clinically distinctive manifestations rather than as evidence of population-level frequency or causal association. The countries contributing the most studies were Singapore (n = 10), followed by India (n = 8), Sri Lanka (n = 7), and Brazil and Taiwan (n = 6 each). Latin American countries (Brazil, Mexico, Colombia, Cuba, Ecuador, and Guatemala) contributed a combined 17 of 62 studies (27%), underscoring a persistent regional evidence gap relative to the region's dengue burden. Publications on chronic post-dengue sequelae have increased markedly in recent years, with 2025-2026 contributing the largest population-based cohort study on this topic to date [7] and the first population-level two-year disability-adjusted life-year (DALY) burden estimate [8]. Distribution by Complication Type Across the 62 included studies, neurological complications were the most frequently represented (30.6%, n = 19), followed by ophthalmological (19.4%, n = 12), heterogeneous persistent symptoms (12.9%, n = 8), fatigue-related (9.7%, n = 6), multisystemic (9.7%, n = 6), psychiatric (9.7%, n = 6), cardiological (4.8%, n = 3), and immunological (3.2%, n = 2). These percentages reflect the proportion of included publications addressing each complication category and should not be interpreted as estimates of clinical prevalence, incidence, or relative risk among dengue patients; approximately one-third of the included studies were case reports or case series, which are not designed to estimate population-level frequency. The multisystemic and psychiatric categories are substantially strengthened by recent large-cohort and review-level evidence, discussed in the corresponding sections below. Complications by system Cardiovascular Complications Three studies addressed chronic cardiovascular sequelae following dengue infection (Table 2), converging on structural and functional myocardial involvement without a consistent relationship to dengue severity: proposed mechanisms include hydroelectrolytic imbalance, hypoperfusion, and lactic acidosis, leading to right ventricular dilatation, tricuspid regurgitation, and arrhythmias, alongside detectable echocardiographic myocardial alterations with a male predominance [4,9]; a broader multi-pathogen review of post-infectious sequelae, in which dengue was discussed among several arboviruses, corroborated susceptibility to similar cardiac sequelae [2]. These mechanistic findings are consistent with population-level data from the Singapore national registry, which reported a 46% higher post-acute cardiovascular risk (see Multisystemic Complications section below) [7]; because this estimate derives from the same registry discussed throughout the Multisystemic section, it should be regarded as hypothesis-strengthening rather than independent external confirmation. Post-Dengue Fatigue Six studies examined fatigue as a chronic post-dengue complication (Table 3). Among the primary cohort studies, reported prevalence ranged widely (17.3-81.5%) depending on follow-up duration and case definition: Perera et al. title: Perfil clínico-epidemiológico dos casos de dengue em cinco regiões de Mineiros, GO, Brasil
abstract: RESUMO A dengue é uma doença não contagiosa causada por um vírus com quatro sorotipos (DENV-1 a DENV-4), transmitida pela fêmea infectada do mosquito Aedes aegypti. Manifesta-se de forma assintomática ou sintomática, sendo a febre o principal sintoma, associada a pelo menos mais dois sinais comuns. A pesquisa teve como objetivo descrever o perfil clínico-epidemiológico da dengue em cinco regiões de Mineiros, GO, em 2024, analisando manifestações clínicas, faixa etária, sexo, sorologia predominante, áreas mais afetadas e locais com maior incidência de casos. Realizou-se um estudo descritivo-exploratório quali-quantitativo, com dados coletados de fichas de notificação do Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação (SINAN) e relatórios epidemiológicos, que posteriormente foram transcritos, analisados e sintetizados, com aprovação prévia pelo Comitê de Ética em Pesquisa. Foram notificados 9421 casos de dengue no município, com pico na 10a semana de notificação. Nas cinco regiões analisadas houveram 5361 notificações, com maior frequência relativa apresentada pela Unidade Básica de Saúde (UBS) Dona Sanica. Quanto às características socioeconômico-demográficas, as cinco UBSs apresentaram aspectos prevalentes semelhantes - sexo feminino, não gestantes, pardas, com 2o grau completo, exceto pelo critério de idade. No que se refere às manifestações clínicas, as cinco regiões apresentaram sintomas prevalentes semelhantes - febre, mialgia e cefaleia. Assim como as principais doenças pré-existentes - hipertensão arterial, diabetes e doença ácido-péptica. Conclui-se, portanto, que ainda que cada UBS possui suas singularidades principalmente no que tange ao número de notificações e área abrangente, todos os fatores analisados para traçar o perfil clínico-epidemiológico se mostraram semelhantes entre si.

A pesquisa teve como objetivo descrever o perfil clínico-epidemiológico da dengue em cinco regiões de Mineiros, GO, em 2024, analisando manifestações clínicas, faixa etária, sexo, sorologia predominante, áreas mais afetadas e locais com maior incidência de casos. Realizou-se um estudo descritivo-exploratório quali-quantitativo, com dados coletados de fichas de notificação do Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação (SINAN) e relatórios epidemiológicos, que posteriormente foram transcritos, analisados e sintetizados, com aprovação prévia pelo Comitê de Ética em Pesquisa. Foram notificados 9421 casos de dengue no município, com pico na 10a semana de notificação. Nas cinco regiões analisadas houveram 5361 notificações, com maior frequência relativa apresentada pela Unidade Básica de Saúde (UBS) Dona Sanica. Quanto às características socioeconômico-demográficas, as cinco UBSs apresentaram aspectos prevalentes semelhantes - sexo feminino, não gestantes, pardas, com 2o grau completo, exceto pelo critério de idade. No que se refere às manifestações clínicas, as cinco regiões apresentaram sintomas prevalentes semelhantes - febre, mialgia e cefaleia. Assim como as principais doenças pré-existentes - hipertensão arterial, diabetes e doença ácido-péptica. Conclui-se, portanto, que ainda que cada UBS possui suas singularidades principalmente no que tange ao número de notificações e área abrangente, todos os fatores analisados para traçar o perfil clínico-epidemiológico se mostraram semelhantes entre si.

title: EXPRESS: Cost-effectiveness of a network of lethal ovitraps for dengue control
abstract: One intervention recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO) to control the spread of dengue fever is a network of lethal ovitraps to capture dengue-carrying Aedes mosquitoes. This study introduces a framework to perform a cost-effectiveness analysis of this intervention that incorporates the substantial operational costs entailed in servicing the network, a factor that has been largely ignored in previous analyses. A vector-host compartmental model was used to model the population dynamics of mosquitoes and to estimate the disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) averted from this intervention. Operational costs were estimated through finding the minimum number of workers that had to be employed to travel to and service all the traps at a specified interval of time. We conducted numerical studies in Singapore and Bangkok to demonstrate how our framework can be used both retrospectively to analyze an existing ovitrap network, and prospectively to assess the cost-effectiveness of setting up a hypothetical ovitrap network. In Singapore, the existing 68,000-trap network was cost-effective over a wide range of service intervals, and the status quo interval of 14 days was near-optimal. In Bangkok, a more heterogeneous setting, three additional findings emerged: allocating traps based on population density was consistently cost-effective; district-specific service intervals improved cost-effectiveness by approximately 30% relative to common single interval; and only the 18 densest districts (of 50) could be made individually cost-effective, surfacing a tradeoff between aggregate cost-effectiveness and equitable coverage. These results illustrate the value of incorporating operational considerations into cost-effectiveness analyses of distributed public-health interventions.

title: A Data‐Driven Approach to Predicting Dengue Fever
abstract: Dengue has emerged as a critical global health challenge, contributing to increasing mortality rates and exerting substantial pressure on healthcare systems. In light of this, considerable research efforts have been directed toward the application of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) methodologies to facilitate the early and accurate diagnosis of dengue. After going through many research papers, it was found that support vector machines (SVMs) were the most frequently utilized, featuring in 25% of the studies, followed by Random Forest, which was applied in approximately 15.6% of cases. A noteworthy finding was the superior performance of a variant of SVM, namely, PCA-SVM (poly-5), which achieved an accuracy of 99.52%, sensitivity of 99.75%, and specificity of 99.09%. These findings underscore the promising role of machine learning in enhancing diagnostic precision for dengue. The high-performance metrics reported in several studies suggest that ML-based approaches could serve as effective clinical decision support tools. Future research should focus on validation across larger, diverse datasets and real-world clinical settings to ensure robustness, generalizability, and practical applicability. Dengue disease continues to position a significant global public health concern, with a rising number of reported cases worldwide. As a substantial challenge for local health authorities and the international public health community, effective strategies for detecting and predicting dengue spread are essential to mitigate its impact. In recent years, machine learning (ML) algorithms have emerged as valuable tools for analyzing complex datasets and predicting disease patterns. By harnessing the power of ML, researchers have explored various techniques to improve dengue prediction and enhance public health interventions. Dengue fever is a major public health concern in tropical regions, transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. Predicting the spread of dengue cases based on climate, environmental, and temporal features can assist in early intervention and resource allocation. In this study, we develop a machine learning–based approach using Random Forest regression to predict weekly dengue cases for the cities of San Juan (Puerto Rico) and Iquitos (Peru). Our model leverages weather, satellite, and vegetation index data to forecast disease incidence, with missing data handled through preprocessing and feature engineering. Performance is evaluated using Mean Absolute Error (MAE), the competition metric.

title_zh: 一种用于预测登革热的数据驱动方法
source_body_en: Dengue has emerged as a critical global health challenge, contributing to increasing mortality rates and exerting substantial pressure on healthcare systems. In light of this, considerable research efforts have been directed toward the application of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) methodologies to facilitate the early and accurate diagnosis of dengue. After going through many research papers, it was found that support vector machines (SVMs) were the most frequently utilized, featuring in 25% of the studies, followed by Random Forest, which was applied in approximately 15.6% of cases. A noteworthy finding was the superior performance of a variant of SVM, namely, PCA-SVM (poly-5), which achieved an accuracy of 99.52%, sensitivity of 99.75%, and specificity of 99.09%. These findings underscore the promising role of machine learning in enhancing diagnostic precision for dengue. The high-performance metrics reported in several studies suggest that ML-based approaches could serve as effective clinical decision support tools. Future research should focus on validation across larger, diverse datasets and real-world clinical settings to ensure robustness, generalizability, and practical applicability. Dengue disease continues to position a significant global public health concern, with a rising number of reported cases worldwide. As a substantial challenge for local health authorities and the international public health community, effective strategies for detecting and predicting dengue spread are essential to mitigate its impact. In recent years, machine learning (ML) algorithms have emerged as valuable tools for analyzing complex datasets and predicting disease patterns. By harnessing the power of ML, researchers have explored various techniques to improve dengue prediction and enhance public health interventions. Dengue fever is a major public health concern in tropical regions, transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. Predicting the spread of dengue cases based on climate, environmental, and temporal features can assist in early intervention and resource allocation. In this study, we develop a machine learning–based approach using Random Forest regression to predict weekly dengue cases for the cities of San Juan (Puerto Rico) and Iquitos (Peru). Our model leverages weather, satellite, and vegetation index data to forecast disease incidence, with missing data handled through preprocessing and feature engineering. Performance is evaluated using Mean Absolute Error (MAE), the competition metric.
abstract_zh: 登革热已成为一个重要的全球健康挑战,导致死亡率率上升,并对医疗保健系统造成巨大压力。鉴于此,大量研究工作已致力于将机器学习(ML)和深度学习(DL)方法应用于登革热的早期和准确诊断。在查阅了许多研究论文后,发现支持媒介机器(SVMs)是最常被使用的,出现在25%的研究中,其次是随机森林,其应用比例约为15.6%。一个值得注意的发现是SVM的一种变体,即PCA-SVM(poly-5),其表现优于其他方法,准确率为99.52%,灵敏度为99.75%,特异度为99.09%。这些发现突显了机器学习在提高登革热诊断精确度方面的前景。一些研究中报告的高性能指标表明,基于机器学习的方法可以作为有效的临床决策支持工具。未来的研究应侧重于在更大、更多样化的数据集和真实世界临床环境中进行验证,以确保其稳健性、可推广性和实际应用价值。登革热疾病继续构成全球公共卫生的重要问题,全球报告的病例数量正在上升。作为对地方卫生当局和国际公共卫生界的重大挑战,有效的登革热检测和预测传播策略对于减轻其影响至关重要。近年来,机器学习(ML)算法已成为分析复杂数据集和预测疾病模式的宝贵工具。通过利用机器学习的力量,研究人员已经探索了多种技术以改进登革热预测并增强公共卫生干预措施。登革热是热带地区的主要公共卫生问题,主要通过Aedes aegypti蚊子传播。基于气候、环境和时间特征预测登革热病例的传播,有助于早期干预和资源分配。在本研究中,我们开发了一种基于机器学习的方法,使用随机森林回归来预测波多黎各圣胡安市和秘鲁伊基托斯市的每周登革热病例。我们的模型利用天气、卫星和植被指数数据来预测疾病发病率,并通过预处理和特征工程处理缺失数据。模型性能通过平均绝对误差(MAE)和竞赛指标进行评估。

title: Antiviral Sesquiterpene Lactones from Laurus nobilis L.: Inhibition of Hepatitis C Virus and Dengue Virus Replication
abstract: Natural products remain indispensable scaffolds in antiviral drug discovery, particularly against high-burden viral pathogens. In this study, two major sesquiterpene lactones, dehydrocostus lactone (1) and costunolide (2), were isolated from Laurus nobilis L. leaves and evaluated for their antiviral potential against hepatitis C virus (HCV) and dengue virus (DENV). The structures of both compounds were confirmed by HRMS and 1D NMR spectroscopic analyses. In subgenomic replicon assays, the molecules inhibited HCV replication in the low-micromolar range (EC50 = 2.34 μM for 1 and 2.06 μM for 2) with favorable selectivity indices. In full-length HCV reporter systems, costunolide (2) displayed enhanced anti-HCV potency, reduced viral RNA and NS5A protein levels, and enhanced the suppressive effect of the clinically approved NS5A inhibitor, daclatasvir. Furthermore, costunolide (2) exhibited cross-flaviviridae activity, suppressing DENV replication (EC50 = 5.89 μM in replicon cells; EC50 = 1.27 μM post-infection in infectious virus assays), and demonstrated cooperative suppression of viral propagation along with reduced glutathione. Mechanistically, these results highlight the critical role of the sesquiterpene lactone core, and the observed enhanced combined activity between costunolide and reduced glutathione is consistent with a possible contribution of the NRF2/glutathione antioxidant axis to its anti-DENV action. Overall, this study highlights L. nobilis as a previously underexplored source of antiviral sesquiterpene lactones and establishes costunolide (2) as a promising lead against HCV and DENV, warranting further investigation across additional Flaviviridae members.

title: Expansion of Dengue Virus Serotype 3 Genetic Diversity and Changing Serotype Composition in Brazil
abstract: Brazil is the most hyperendemic country for dengue, with historically dominant circulation of DENV-1 and DENV-2. Bayesian phylodynamic analyses of 489 Brazilian DENV-3 genomes, including 84 newly generated sequences, reveal a recent and sustained increase in the effective population size of DENV-3 associated with the recent introduction and expansion of the 3III_B.3.2 lineage. This increase coincides with a sharp rise in the proportion of laboratory-confirmed dengue cases attributed to DENV-3 among records with available serotype information from 2024 onwards and a shift in serotype dynamics in 2025, suggesting a change in serotype distribution and a potential risk of renewed DENV-3 outbreaks, particularly in populations with limited prior exposure to this serotype.
authors: Arabela Leal E Silva de Mello

title: Analysis of Dengue Epidemic Model with Optimal Control Strategies
abstract: Dengue is virus which is caused by aedes Agypti mosquito the can transmitted by this vec tors.The global dynamics and control strategies of an epidemic model system for dengue and we analyze the model considering the controls as constants. The biological feasibility of the model system is examined. The existence and stability of the equilibrium states are studied concerning the basic reproduction number. Both the local and the global asymp totic stability of the system’s equilibrium states are considered. Next, we introduce the time-dependent controls, namely, personal prevention for dengue infection, treatment for the infected persons, and environmental hygiene against Dengue into the model. A con trol problem is proposed and solved analytically. The necessary conditions for the effective control of the disease are derived by applying Pontryagin’s maximum principle. Moreover, several possible combinations of the controls are considered, and also their productiveness is compared through the several numerical illustrations. It is suggested from the simulation works that the best strategy to minimize the transmission of dengue virus is to adopt all the three controls optimally among the considered strategies. Findings: Results indicate that reducing mosquito biting rates and increasing human recovery rates are effective strategies for controlling dengue transmission. The model exhibits backward bifurcation, suggesting that even when R0 is less than one, the disease can persist in the population under certain conditions. Novelty: This study presents a novel modeling framework that can inform the development of targeted prevention and management strategies for dengue. Keywords: Dengue fever, Mathematical Modeling, Ordinary differential equations, Basic reproduction number, Sensitivity analysis, Optimal control.
journal: National Academic Digital Repository of Ethiopia

A con trol problem is proposed and solved analytically. The necessary conditions for the effective control of the disease are derived by applying Pontryagin’s maximum principle. Moreover, several possible combinations of the controls are considered, and also their productiveness is compared through the several numerical illustrations. It is suggested from the simulation works that the best strategy to minimize the transmission of dengue virus is to adopt all the three controls optimally among the considered strategies. Findings: Results indicate that reducing mosquito biting rates and increasing human recovery rates are effective strategies for controlling dengue transmission. The model exhibits backward bifurcation, suggesting that even when R0 is less than one, the disease can persist in the population under certain conditions. Novelty: This study presents a novel modeling framework that can inform the development of targeted prevention and management strategies for dengue. Keywords: Dengue fever, Mathematical Modeling, Ordinary differential equations, Basic reproduction number, Sensitivity analysis, Optimal control.

title: Trophoblast metabolic reprogramming triggers adverse pregnancy outcomes during DENV-2 infection in mice
abstract: ABSTRACT Adverse pregnancy outcomes associated with dengue virus (DENV) infection are a severe manifestation of dengue fever; however, we still poorly understand the underlying mechanisms. Trophoblast dysfunction in the placenta contributes centrally to various pregnancy complications. As the functional unit of the placenta, the syncytiotrophoblast (STB) requires continuous fusion of precursor trophoblasts and adequate energy supply. In this study, we established a model of adverse pregnancy by infecting Ifnar 1 −/− pregnant mice with DENV-2. We did not detect viral replication within the placental trophoblast layer but observed substantial structural damage to the STB. RNA-seq analysis demonstrated that precursor trophoblasts exhibit disrupted glucose metabolism, and placental tissue upregulates pro-fusion genes—yet fails to complete syncytialization. Metabolic assays revealed reduced ATP levels and elevated lactate concentrations, indicating that an inadequate energy supply impedes trophoblast differentiation. Treatment with the glycolytic inhibitor 2-DG restored oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) activity in the placenta and markedly improved pathological outcomes. Further mechanistic studies established that DENV infection induces oxidative stress, which activates hypoxia-inducible factor Hif1α, leading to subsequent upregulation of lactate dehydrogenase (LDHA) expression. We identify this cascade as a fundamental mechanism underlying metabolic reprogramming in trophoblasts. Our findings not only clarify the key pathological processes driving DENV-induced adverse pregnancy outcomes but also propose novel therapeutic strategies for clinical intervention. IMPORTANCE Dengue virus infection during pregnancy is linked to adverse fetal outcomes, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In Ifnar 1 −/− pregnant mice, we show that fetal growth restriction is driven by disruption of the maternal environment that impairs placental function. We identify syncytiotrophoblast damage and defective trophoblast fusion despite compensatory upregulation of pro-fusion genes. Placental metabolic analysis reveals a shift from oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis, accompanied by reduced ATP production and impaired syncytialization. Inhibition of glycolysis in vivo partially restores placental structure and improves fetal outcomes, supporting a key role for metabolic reprogramming. Mechanistically, ROS activates HIF-1α and upregulates its downstream target LDHA, thereby linking metabolic reprogramming to placental dysfunction and highlighting this pathway as a potential therapeutic target. These findings reveal a mechanism underlying DENV-associated pregnancy complications and highlight metabolic pathways as potential therapeutic targets.

title: Clinical presentation of Dengue fever in children in a tertiary care hospital
abstract: Background: Dengue fever is a very common tropical disease and also a major public concern in Bangladesh. It occurs in Bangladesh during and just after the rainy season. The risk factors of Dengue fever are environmental and climatic situation. Clinical manifestations of Dengue in children often vary. So, making early diagnosis of Dengue is very challenging. Objective: To evaluate the clinical presentation of Dengue fever in children admitted to a tertiary care hospital in Bangladesh. Methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted in the paediatric department of a Bangladesh Medical University over a six months period from July 2024 to December 2024. Fifty Children aged 6 months to 15 years were included. Results: The majority of children belonged to the 5-10-year age group. Most patients (64.0%) were from urban areas, and males were predominantly affected (58.0%). The most common clinical features were fever (100.0%), abdominal pain (62.0%), vomiting (58.0%), rash (44.0%), diarrhoea (24.0%) and bleeding manifestations (44.0%). A positive tourniquet test was observed in 68.0% of cases. Pleural effusion and ascites were found in 16.0% and 28.0% of patients, respectively. Regarding disease severity, 18.0% had Dengue fever, 38.0% had Dengue hemorrhagic fever, 20.0% had Dengue with warning signs and 24.0% presented with Dengue shock syndrome. Conclusion: Dengue fever in children presents with a wide spectrum of clinical features, ranging from mild febrile illness to severe life-threatening complications. DS (Child) H J 2025; 41(1): 7-10

title: Hubungan Peran Kepala Keluarga Dan Kader Jumantik dengan Perilaku Pencegahan Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) Di Dusun Biting 2 Desa Kutorenon Lumajang
abstract: Demam Berdarah Dengue (DHF) masih menjadi masalah kesehatan masyarakat yang berkaitan dengan perilaku pencegahan masyarakat. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis hubungan peran kepala keluarga dan kader Jumantik dengan perilaku pencegahan DHF di Biting 2, Kutorenon, Lumajang. Penelitian kuantitatif korelasional dengan pendekatan cross-sectional melibatkan 213 responden yang dipilih secara proportional random sampling. Data dianalisis menggunakan uji Spearman Rank. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan peran kepala keluarga sebagian besar berkategori sedang (47,9%), sedangkan peran kader Jumantik (45,1%) dan perilaku pencegahan DHF (54,0%) sebagian besar berkategori baik. Terdapat hubungan positif yang kuat antara peran kepala keluarga dengan perilaku pencegahan DHF (r = 0,710; p < 0,001) serta antara peran kader Jumantik dengan perilaku pencegahan DHF (r = 0,724; p < 0,001). Puskesmas disarankan mengintegrasikan program edukasi terarah bagi kepala keluarga sebagai pengambil keputusan rumah tangga, serta memperkuat pembinaan dan penyediaan media edukasi visual bagi kader Jumantik dalam menggerakkan aksi nyata PSN 3M Plus secara konsisten.

title: Spatial interactions of urban poverty and livestock environments with dengue incidence: A Bivariate Moran's I Analysis in Denpasar, Bali.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) remains a major public health problem in tropical regions, including Indonesia. Its transmission is influenced by complex interactions between environmental, animal, and human factors. This study applies a One Health approach to examine spatial interactions between livestock environments, urban conditions, and dengue incidence in Denpasar, Bali. METHODS This study used a cross-sectional spatial design at the subdistrict level, using secondary data from 2025. Dengue cases were analyzed as the dependent variable, while the number of pig farmers and slum areas represented animal and environmental factors, respectively. Spatial analysis was conducted using QGIS and GeoDa, applying Bivariate Moran's I and BiLISA to identify global and local spatial relationships. RESULTS The analysis showed a significant positive spatial association between the number of pig farmers and dengue incidence (Moran's I = 0.127; p = 0.041), indicating a clustering pattern. Slum areas were not significantly associated with dengue incidence (p = 0.487). Local analysis identified a High-High cluster in Padangsambian Kaja and several Low-High clusters, suggesting potential spatial spillover effects between neighboring areas. DISCUSSION The findings indicate that livestock-related environments may indirectly influence dengue transmission by creating conditions favorable for mosquito breeding. The presence of spatial clustering and spillover effects highlights the importance of considering interregional connectivity and environmental context in disease control strategies. CONCLUSION Dengue distribution in Denpasar is shaped by spatial and environmental dynamics, particularly livestock-related factors. Targeted, spatially informed interventions using a One Health approach are essential to improve the effectiveness of dengue prevention and control.

title: MODELAGEM MATEMÁTICA DOS CASOS DE DENGUE NO RIO GRANDE DO SUL: COMPARAÇÃO ENTRE OS MODELOS DE GOMPERTZ, RICHARDS E POLINOMIAL MATHEMATICAL MODELING OF DENGUE CASES IN RIO GRANDE DO SUL: A COMPARISON OF THE GOMPERTZ, RICHARDS, AND POLYNOMIAL MODELS
abstract: A dengue constitui um relevante problema de saúde pública, apresentando variações expressivas no número de casos ao longo do tempo. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar os casos confirmados de dengue no Rio Grande do Sul entre 2015 e 2025, mediante o ajuste dos modelos de Gompertz e Richards com parâmetro adicional para o ano de 2024, bem como de um modelo polinomial de grau 10. A pesquisa caracteriza-se como quantitativa, documental e descritiva, utilizando dados obtidos no Painel de Casos de Dengue da Secretaria da Saúde do Estado do Rio Grande do Sul. Os parâmetros dos modelos de Gompertz e Richards foram estimados em linguagem Python pelo método dos mínimos quadrados não lineares, enquanto o modelo polinomial foi determinado pela interpolação dos 11 pontos observados. A qualidade dos ajustes foi avaliada pelo coeficiente de determinação (R2). O polinômio de grau 10 apresentou (R2=1,0000), seguido pelos modelos de Richards, com (R2=0,9893), e de Gompertz, com (R2=0,9523). Os três modelos representaram satisfatoriamente os dados, com o modelo polinomial de grau 10 tendo a maior adequação aos dados observados no período analisado.

A pesquisa caracteriza-se como quantitativa, documental e descritiva, utilizando dados obtidos no Painel de Casos de Dengue da Secretaria da Saúde do Estado do Rio Grande do Sul. Os parâmetros dos modelos de Gompertz e Richards foram estimados em linguagem Python pelo método dos mínimos quadrados não lineares, enquanto o modelo polinomial foi determinado pela interpolação dos 11 pontos observados. A qualidade dos ajustes foi avaliada pelo coeficiente de determinação (R2). O polinômio de grau 10 apresentou (R2=1,0000), seguido pelos modelos de Richards, com (R2=0,9893), e de Gompertz, com (R2=0,9523). Os três modelos representaram satisfatoriamente os dados, com o modelo polinomial de grau 10 tendo a maior adequação aos dados observados no período analisado.

title: The gut-liver axis and the role of bacteria in severe dengue virus infection in mice
abstract: Patients with severe dengue virus (DENV) infection can experience hemorrhage, shock and organ damage that coincides with defervescence and declining viremia. In addition to vascular leak, published work has shown that gut barrier permeability and elevated serum lipopolysaccharide (LPS) levels correlate with DENV disease severity. We previously described profound gut pathology in a mouse model of infection. This led to the hypothesis that a loss of gut epithelial barrier integrity and the influx of microbial products contribute to exacerbated inflammation and severe dengue disease. Consistent with this, here we demonstrated that DENV2 infection of AG129 mice compromised the gut epithelial barrier, promoted bacterial translocation, and induced microbial changes indicative of dysbiosis, including a reduced abundance of putatively beneficial microbial taxa and disrupted microbial circadian oscillations. Depleting gut bacteria with antibiotics from 1-day post-infection sharply reduced gut pathology as well as viral RNA in the proximal colon and liver, and the number of infected Kupffer cells in the liver. There was no evidence for systemic suppression of viral replication. We propose that viral infection of intestinal macrophages leads to inflammatory damage and mucosal barrier breakdown, dysbiosis and gut leak, with gut bacteria-dependent products promoting the susceptibility of Kupffer cells to DENV infection. Given the importance of liver damage in severe and fatal dengue disease, therapies that protect the gut barrier may help reduce disease severity.

title: MANIFESTAÇÕES NEUROLÓGICAS ASSOCIADAS À INFECÇÃO PELO VÍRUS DA DENGUE NEURODENGUE: NEUROLOGICAL MANIFESTATIONS ASSOCIATED WITH DENGUE VIRUS INFECTION NEURODENGUE: MANIFESTACIONES NEUROLÓGICAS ASOCIADAS A LA INFECCIÓN POR EL VIRUS DEL DENGUE
abstract: O termo neurodengue refere-se às manifestações neurológicas decorrentes da infecção pelo vírus da dengue, cuja frequência tem aumentado paralelamente à crescente incidência da doença. O acometimento pode envolver tanto o sistema nervoso central quanto o periférico, ocasionando quadros como encefalopatia e encefalite, além de outras complicações neurológicas potencialmente graves e incapacitantes. Esta revisão tem como finalidade abordar as complicações neurológicas relacionadas à dengue, enfatizando os mecanismos fisiopatológicos, as manifestações clínicas e os principais desafios envolvidos no diagnóstico. Teve como objetivo ampliar o conhecimento sobre essas afecções graves, ainda pouco reconhecidas, contribuindo para o diagnóstico precoce e o manejo adequado dos pacientes. Assim, realizou-se uma busca bibliográfica nas bases de dados PubMed e Biblioteca Virtual em Saúde (BVS), por meio dos descritores "dengue fever" e "neurological manifestations", disponíveis nos Descritores em Ciência da Saúde (DeCS), combinados pelo operador booleano “AND”, publicados nos últimos 10 anos, sendo selecionados 15 artigos para fundamentar o presente estudo. Os achados demonstram a diversidade das manifestações neurológicas relacionadas à dengue e ressaltam a complexidade de seu diagnóstico, especialmente diante da sobreposição de sinais e sintomas com outras condições neurológicas. Dessa forma, o reconhecimento dessas complicações e a compreensão de seus aspectos clínicos e fisiopatológicos são essenciais para uma abordagem adequada dos pacientes e para a prevenção de desfechos desfavoráveis.

title: Environmental Decision-Making Under Abrupt Transformation: Lessons from the Nova Kakhovka Dam Breach and Data-Driven Dengue Control
abstract: Abrupt environmental transformations create two simultaneous problems: rapid change in the physical system and disruption of the data required to understand and manage it. This contribution examines this challenge through two contrasting cases. The first is the catastrophic breach of the Nova Kakhovka Dam in Ukraine on 6 June 2023, which drained the reservoir, interrupted irrigation, flooded downstream areas and mobilised pollution. A rapid assessment after the breach shows what could be established from available information, which concerns required further analysis, and how data quality affected interpretation and decision-making. The second case concerns data-driven dengue control in endemic countries. Disease surveillance, mosquito-vector control and hospital preparedness depend on near-real-time information on cases, serotypes, climate and environmental conditions, supported by historical records. Population displacement, conflict, lockdowns and interrupted monitoring can change transmission conditions while weakening the information systems used to respond. The cases are not presented as environmentally equivalent. Their methodological connection is a decision problem: maintaining defensible analysis when both the monitored system and the evidence infrastructure change. The presentation argues that resilience requires baselines, preparation for interrupted data streams and explicit treatment of uncertainty in environmental and public-health decisions.

title: Efectividad de las intervenciones educativas dirigidas a la prevención del dengue en comunidades de Manabí Effectiveness of educational interventions aimed at dengue prevention in Manabí communities
abstract: El dengue constituye una de las principales enfermedades virales transmitidas por vectores y representa un problema de salud pública, especialmente en comunidades donde persisten condiciones que favorecen la presencia de Aedes aegypti. La educación para la salud constituye una estrategia importante para fortalecer los conocimientos y promover prácticas orientadas a la prevención y el control del vector. El objetivo de esta revisión fue evaluar la efectividad de las intervenciones educativas dirigidas a la prevención del dengue en comunidades de Manabí. Se desarrolló una revisión sistemática y documental de tipo descriptivo, mediante la búsqueda de publicaciones científicas correspondientes al periodo 2021-2026 en PubMed, Scopus, SciELO, Google Académico, ScienceDirect, Dialnet y Redalyc. Se consideraron estudios relacionados con dengue, educación para la salud, intervenciones educativas, prevención y control vectorial. Los resultados evidenciaron diferencias en el nivel de conocimiento sobre el dengue, con valores de conocimiento adecuado que oscilaron entre 24,6 % y 87,8 %. Las intervenciones identificadas incluyeron programas educativos escolares, charlas, sesiones comunitarias, métodos participativos y materiales didácticos. La efectividad reportada osciló entre 75 % y 96,42 %, observándose mejoras en el conocimiento y en las prácticas preventivas después de las intervenciones. En conclusión, la evidencia revisada muestra que las intervenciones educativas pueden contribuir al fortalecimiento de los conocimientos y las prácticas relacionadas con la prevención del dengue, por lo que su aplicación debe considerar las características y necesidades de cada comunidad.

Las intervenciones identificadas incluyeron programas educativos escolares, charlas, sesiones comunitarias, métodos participativos y materiales didácticos. La efectividad reportada osciló entre 75 % y 96,42 %, observándose mejoras en el conocimiento y en las prácticas preventivas después de las intervenciones. En conclusión, la evidencia revisada muestra que las intervenciones educativas pueden contribuir al fortalecimiento de los conocimientos y las prácticas relacionadas con la prevención del dengue, por lo que su aplicación debe considerar las características y necesidades de cada comunidad.

title: Modelling Dengue Transmission Dynamics using a Two-Time Delay Differential Equation
abstract: This study proposes an autonomous dynamical system to model the transmission dynamics of dengue epidemic, using a two – time delay differential equation. The delay due to extrinsic and intrinsic incubation period for the host (humans) and vector (mosquitoes) was considered. The existence of the equilibrium points was investigated and its stability studied analytically. The endemic equilibrium was found to be stable if the delay is under certain conditions. Numerical simulations were performed to obtain numerical results for the basic reproduction number with both time delays for a range of parameter values, to illustrate the theoretical results.
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF APPLIED SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICAL THEORY

title: Edukasi dan Pelatihan Pembuatan Ovitrap sebagai Upaya Pencegahan Demam Berdarah Dengue
abstract: Demam Berdarah Dengue (DBD) masih menjadi persoalan kesehatan lingkungan yang membutuhkan keterlibatan masyarakat dalam pengendalian nyamuk Aedes. Kegiatan ini bertujuan meningkatkan pemahaman dan keterampilan masyarakat mengenai pencegahan DBD melalui edukasi, demonstrasi, dan praktik pembuatan ovitrap sederhana. Kegiatan dilaksanakan di RW 10 Kelurahan Karang Rejo, Kecamatan Metro Utara, Kota Metro dengan melibatkan 20 peserta. Pelaksanaan menggunakan pendekatan pendidikan masyarakat dan pelatihan, sedangkan evaluasi dilakukan dengan rancangan one group pre-test post-test. Instrumen berupa kuesioner diberikan sebelum dan sesudah kegiatan. Data dianalisis secara deskriptif dan dilanjutkan dengan Paired Samples T-Test. Hasil menunjukkan rata-rata skor peserta meningkat dari 12,90 pada pre-test menjadi 14,90 pada post-test. Perbedaan skor menunjukkan hasil yang signifikan dengan nilai p < 0,001. Peserta memperoleh materi mengenai DBD dan ovitrap serta mengikuti demonstrasi dan praktik pembuatan alat. Kegiatan ini menunjukkan bahwa edukasi yang dipadukan dengan praktik dapat mendukung pemberdayaan masyarakat dalam pencegahan DBD. Ovitrap dalam kegiatan ini diposisikan sebagai metode pendukung PSN 3M Plus, sehingga penerapannya tetap perlu disertai pengelolaan lingkungan secara rutin.

title: Dengue fever model with impulsive intervention in a periodically varying environment
abstract: Pulse interventions represent a highly effective measure for infection control, as they influence disease transmission through short-term actions. In addition, the habitat ranges of dengue vectors and hosts exhibit periodic variations driven by environmental and climatic factors. To investigate the effects of impulsive interventions and domain evolution on disease transmission, we propose a dengue fever reaction-diffusion model that incorporates impulsive perturbations in a periodically varying domain. By applying the Poincar$\acute{e}$ map and the Krein-Rutman theorem, we establish the existence of the principal eigenvalue for the periodic eigenvalue problem with impulses, thereby extending previous studies on reaction-diffusion equations in fixed domains without impulsive effects. Sufficient conditions governing the long-term dynamics of periodic solutions are derived using the comparison principle and monotone iteration theory. Numerical simulations corroborate the theoretical findings and elucidate the effects of impulsive-intervention intensity and periodic domain evolution on disease transmission patterns. Our results indicate that increasing the intensity of pulse interventions suppresses disease transmission, whereas a larger magnitude of domain variation impedes disease control.

title: Analysis of Dengue Fever Data using Neighborhood Based Infra-Topological Approximation Spaces
abstract: With an objective to enhance the approximation space, this paper integrates an infra-topological structure with three distinct neighborhood systems: j, j-adhesion and Ej neighborhoods. The infra-topological structure is less rigorous than classical topological spaces and offers greater flexibility in modeling uncertainty and vagueness. It has applications in attribute reduction, medical diagnosis, granular computing, etc. אj, j-adhesion and Ej-infra-topological spaces are introduced from the corresponding neighborhood systems under the binary relation. The relationships between infra-topologies are investigated under the binary relation. These infra-topologies are subsequently utilized to define the infra-אj, infra-j-adhesion and infra-Ej approximation operators. The key benefit of these models is that they maintain the properties of Pawlak approximation operators. A distinctive feature of the current approach is that all accuracy measures remain identical (one) when applied under a reflexive relation. The dengue fever information system is analyzed by proposed methods, which effectively reduce the diagnostic vagueness and improve decision-making. The strengths and limitations of the current approaches are mentioned in the paper.
