License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ An Adaptive Gated Fusion-based Multimodal Framework for Influential Actor Identification in Dengue Haemorrhagic Fever Information Dissemination on YouTube Ayu Eka Lestari1 Wiwik Anggraeni1* 1Department of Information Systems, Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember, Surabaya, Indonesia * Corresponding author’s Email: wiwik@is.its.ac.id Abstract: Dengue hemorrhagic fever remains a critical public health concern in Indonesia, and YouTube has become a major channel for health information. Identifying influential actors is essential for public health communication, yet existing social network analysis relies on text and ignores visual signals such as video thumbnails. This study proposes a multimodal framework based on Adaptive Gated Fusion that combines text and visual features without any audio modality. Textual features from IndoBERT and visual features from ResNet-50 are fused adaptively per dimension, aggregated per channel, and used to build a content-based co-audience network analysed with PageRank. Using 33,233 Indonesian comments from 5,365 videos across 1,129 collected channels (1,084 retained after language filtering) over 2021 to 2025, an ablation study with stratified five-fold cross-validation shows the fused representation reaches 79.52 percent accuracy and 78.42 percent macro F1, outperforming text and visual baselines. KOMPASTV, Kata Dokter, and Halodoc emerged as the most influential actors. Keywords: Adaptive gated fusion, Co-audience graph, Dengue haemorrhagic fever, IndoBERT, PageRank, ResNet- 50, Sentiment analysis, Social network analysis, YouTube. 1. Introduction Dengue haemorrhagic fever (DHF) is a tropical infectious disease transmitted through the bites of the Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes, and it is one of the major public health burdens in Indonesia. The World Health Organization (WHO) recorded 149,866 confirmed DHF cases in Indonesia up to 1 July 2024, an increase of roughly threefold compared with the same period in 2023, spread across 465 regencies/cities in 38 provinces [1]. Although the case trend declined in 2025, DHF remains a health priority that requires effective prevention strategies and public education [2]. As case numbers rise, the Indonesian public increasingly relies on social media as a source of health information. YouTube has a unique characteristic as a multimodal platform: its content combines visual elements in the form of video thumbnails and textual elements in the form of user comments, which jointly shape public health perceptions and behaviour [3]. However, the openness of this platform also presents challenges, because the information that circulates is not always accurate and can negatively affect public health decisions [4]. Identifying the most influential actors in the dissemination of DHF information is crucial for designing well-targeted interventions. Social Network Analysis (SNA) has proven effective for this purpose: centrality metrics such as PageRank, degree centrality, and betweenness centrality are widely used to measure the level of influence of a node in a network [5], while community detection through the Louvain algorithm enables actors to be grouped according to similar interaction patterns [6]. However, previous research applying SNA to health information has been dominated by text-based platforms such as Twitter and Facebook [7]. As a result, when influence is measured solely from textual signals, the visual dimension that also Received: June 18, 2026. Revised: July 16, 2026. 669 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.34 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ determines the reach of content, particularly thumbnails on platforms such as YouTube, is entirely overlooked. On multimodal platforms, measuring influence from text alone risks misjudging which actors shape public discourse, so a representation capable of capturing both modalities simultaneously is needed. In natural language processing, pre-trained transformer-based models such as BERT have transformed the way text is represented, and IndoBERT in particular is able to understand the context of the Indonesian language better than multilingual models [8]; this capability has been exploited for sentiment analysis of YouTube comments [9] and emotion classification [10]. In computer vision, ResNet-50 is a deep learning architecture widely used for visual feature extraction because its residual learning approach enables the construction of deep networks with effective training [11]. Multimodal approaches that fuse textual and visual features have been shown to improve analytical accuracy compared with unimodal approaches [12]. In particular, the Adaptive Gated Fusion (AGF) technique combines the two modalities through a gating mechanism that assigns dynamic per-dimension weights between text and visual features [13], so that the contribution of each modality is not set uniformly but is adjusted to the characteristics of each piece of content. AGF therefore has the potential to address the limitations of text-based analysis by integrating the visual signals that have so far been ignored in identifying influential actors on multimodal platforms. Based on the review above, two main gaps can be identified. First, studies on influential actors in health information still focus on text-based platforms, whereas YouTube, which combines text and visuals, has not been widely studied. Second, SNA research generally still uses only a single type of data, so the visual information in video content has not been optimally exploited; in particular, the combination of IndoBERT and ResNet-50 through adaptive fusion to build a co-audience network has never been explored. To address these gaps, this study proposes an AGF- based multimodal framework for identifying influential actors in the dissemination of DHF information on YouTube. The main objectives of this study are described as follows: 1. Multimodal Representation: integrating IndoBERT textual embeddings and ResNet-50 visual embeddings through Adaptive Gated Fusion (AGF), which assigns adaptive per- dimension weights across modalities, without relying on the audio modality. 2. Network Construction: building a co-audience graph based on multimodal content similarity derived from AGF, rather than explicit interactions, and applying PageRank-based SNA to identify influential channels together with their community structure. 3. Sentiment Profiling: fine-tuning a RoBERTa model for Indonesian text to build sentiment profiles for each influential channel. 4. Empirical Validation: conducting an ablation study with stratified 5-fold cross-validation on seven modality configurations to evaluate whether the adaptively fused multimodal representation outperforms the unimodal text and visual baselines in sentiment classification accuracy. The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. Section 2 reviews related works on multimodal sentiment analysis, social network analysis, and sentiment analysis of health content. Section 3 describes the dataset and the proposed AGF-based multimodal framework. Section 4 presents the experimental results and discussion. Finally, Section 5 concludes the paper and outlines directions for future work. 2. Related works 2.1 Multimodal sentiment analysis Multimodal sentiment analysis combines information from several modalities, typically text, audio, and visual, to produce a richer representation than a single modality alone. Gandhi et al. [14] concluded that multimodal fusion methods outperform unimodal approaches across various datasets, and Zhu et al. [15] reinforced this finding through a survey of fusion methods that emphasised that selecting the appropriate fusion strategy is highly decisive for model performance. In a domain similar to this study, Kothuri and RajaLakshmi [16] proposed the MALO-LSTM model, which combines text, audio, and visual modalities for sentiment analysis on YouTube; the model achieved 98.62% accuracy and showed that combining the three modalities yields better results than using the modalities separately. Recent research emphasises the importance of adaptive fusion mechanisms, that is, mechanisms that adjust the weight of each modality according to context. Wang et al. [17] proposed a multimodal transformer that assigns modality weights adaptively, whereas Lu et al. [18] developed a gated-fusion- based framework that has been shown to filter signals across modalities through a sigmoid gate that dynamically determines the magnitude of each Received: June 18, 2026. Revised: July 16, 2026. 670 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.34 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ modality's contribution [19]. However, most of these methods were developed for English-language data and still rely on the audio modality, so the potential of the visual modality in the form of thumbnails, the primary signal on platforms such as YouTube, has not been optimally exploited, particularly for Indonesian-language content. 2.2 Social network analysis for influential actor identification Social Network Analysis (SNA) is widely used to identify key actors in online information networks. The PageRank algorithm, originally designed to rank web pages [20] was later adapted to the social network context, measuring the influence of a node not only from the number of connections but also from their quality. Rashidi et al. [21] developed a method to predict influential nodes based on local communities and user reaction information, and the results showed that nodes with high PageRank values tend to be effective information spreaders. Similarly, data-driven frameworks combine several centrality metrics such as degree centrality, betweenness centrality, and PageRank to make node rankings more accurate [22]. In the health context, identifying influential actors is highly important for designing public communication strategies. A qualitative study by Green et al. showed that digital opinion leaders play an important role in disseminating dengue prevention information, including in Indonesia [23]. However, most studies still build relationships between users from explicit interactions such as retweets and mentions, even though users who discuss similar topics do not necessarily interact with one another. Therefore, approaches based on multimodal embeddings that can capture content similarity remain underexplored. 2.3 Sentiment analysis of health content on social media Sentiment analysis of health content on social media can provide insight into how the public perceives a disease. In the case of dengue, Laguitan et al. [24] found that the quality and reliability of information circulating on YouTube vary widely, so not all sources have the same credibility and it is important to identify trustworthy sources. In Indonesia, Putri et al. [25] used IndoBERT to analyse public sentiment toward various public issues, whereas Mahakerty et al. [26] integrated Indonesian- language Twitter sentiment analysis into a deep- learning-based disease prediction model. These findings show that sentiment analysis can serve as a useful supplementary source of information for understanding the dynamics of disease spread in society. 2.4 Research gap Based on the literature review above, there are three research gaps centred on the suboptimal use of multimodal representations. First, research on multimodal sentiment analysis is still dominated by English-language data and rarely focuses on the Indonesian language, particularly in the health domain. Second, most multimodal methods rely on the audio modality, whereas the combination of text and visual thumbnails, which is precisely the primary signal on platforms such as YouTube, has not been widely studied. Third, the construction of co- audience networks to identify influential actors still depends on explicit interactions and has not exploited cross-modal content similarity, so the visual dimension that also determines content reach is overlooked. These gaps underscore the need for an Indonesian-language multimodal framework that explicitly combines the text and visual modalities to identify influential actors in the dissemination of dengue information on YouTube. Unlike previous research, the main novelty of this study lies in integrating IndoBERT text representations and ResNet-50 thumbnail visual features through Adaptive Gated Fusion (AGF), which assigns adaptive per-dimension weights across modalities without relying on the audio modality. The resulting multimodal fused representation is then used to build a co-audience network based on content similarity rather than explicit interactions, and the contribution of each modality is verified through an ablation study so that the advantage of the multimodal approach can be demonstrated empirically against the unimodal text and visual baselines. 3. Material and method This section describes the dataset and the research procedure used to identify influential actors in the dissemination of dengue haemorrhagic fever (DHF) information on YouTube through a multimodal approach. The overall research workflow is presented in Fig. 1. 3.1 Dataset This study uses comment data and video thumbnails related to dengue haemorrhagic fever Received: June 18, 2026. The collected raw data came from 5,365 unique videos across 1,129 YouTube channels. Each data entry includes the comment text, video metadata (title, view count, and publication date), and the video thumbnail image. 3.2 Method This study applies a multimodal framework consisting of nine main stages: data collection, preprocessing, feature extraction, multimodal fusion through Adaptive Gated Fusion (AGF), channel-level aggregation, co-audience graph construction, social network analysis, sentiment analysis, and evaluation through an ablation study. The complete research process is shown in Fig. 1. 3.2.1. Preprocessing The preprocessing stage was carried out to produce clean and standardised data. This process comprises four steps. First, noise removal of URLs, mentions (@), hashtags (#), numbers, and special characters. Second, duplicate removal to avoid redundancy. Third, language filtering using the langdetect library to retain only Indonesian language comments. Fourth, removal of comments shorter than five words. After preprocessing, 33,233 valid comments were obtained, or 91.5% of the original corpus, which were then aligned with the related video thumbnails. 3.2.2. Multimodal feature extraction Feature extraction was carried out in parallel for the two modalities. For the text modality, each comment was encoded using IndoBERT (indobert- base-pl) [8] a BERT-based language model trained on a large Indonesian-language corpus. The token representation from the final encoder layer was used as the sentence embedding, producing a 768- dimensional vector for each comment. For the visual modality, each video thumbnail was processed using the ResNet-50 architecture [11] pre-trained on the ImageNet dataset. The final classification layer was removed, so the output taken was a 2,048-dimensional feature vector from the global average pooling layer. Each thumbnail was resized to 224 × 224 pixels before inference. The residual learning approach in ResNet-50 enables the construction of deep networks with effective training [11]. 3.2.3. Multimodal Representation: integrating IndoBERT textual embeddings and ResNet-50 visual embeddings through Adaptive Gated Fusion (AGF), which assigns adaptive per- dimension weights across modalities, without relying on the audio modality. 2. Network Construction: building a co-audience graph based on multimodal content similarity derived from AGF, rather than explicit interactions, and applying PageRank-based SNA to identify influential channels together with their community structure. 3. Sentiment Profiling: fine-tuning a RoBERTa model for Indonesian text to build sentiment profiles for each influential channel. 4. Empirical Validation: conducting an ablation study with stratified 5-fold cross-validation on seven modality configurations to evaluate whether the adaptively fused multimodal representation outperforms the unimodal text and visual baselines in sentiment classification accuracy. The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. Section 2 reviews related works on multimodal sentiment analysis, social network analysis, and sentiment analysis of health content. Section 3 describes the dataset and the proposed AGF-based multimodal framework. Section 4 presents the experimental results and discussion. Finally, Section 5 concludes the paper and outlines directions for future work. 2. analysis.summary_en: This study introduces an adaptive gated fusion-based multimodal framework for identifying influential actors in dengue hemorrhagic fever information dissemination on YouTube. The framework integrates both textual and visual features, using IndoBERT for text and ResNet-50 for visual analysis. The study analyzed 33,233 Indonesian comments from 5,365 videos across 1,129 channels, with 1,084 retained after language filtering. Results showed the framework achieved 79.52 percent accuracy and 78.42 percent macro F1, outperforming text and visual baselines. The evidence strength is moderate due to the regional and platform-specific focus.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,他们的框架通过整合文本和视觉特征,能够有效识别YouTube上登革热出血热信息传播中的有影响力角色,这与现有仅依赖文本的方法相比是一种新颖的途径。

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于印尼的YouTube数据,并依赖于用户评论,这可能无法完全代表更广泛的讨论。由于研究集中在单一平台和区域,证据强度中等。

title: Examining Dengue-related Information Diffusion on Indonesian Twitter Through Sentiment-based Network Analysis, Spatial Mapping, and Temporal Dynamics
abstract: Dengue fever remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, yet studies integrating sentiment analysis, Social Network Analysis, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on social media remain limited.This study proposes an integrated framework applied to 5,715 dengue-related tweets collected from Indonesian Twitter between January 2021 and December 2025.Sentiment classification using IndoBERT revealed a predominantly neutral discourse (65.23%), with meaningful negative (20.31%) and positive (14.45%) proportions.Sentiment-weighted interaction networks were constructed and analysed, revealing highly fragmented structures with modularity scores exceeding 0.98.Healthcare professionals emerged as the most robustly influential actors by betweenness centrality, with PageRank-based influence conditional on self-loop treatment, while the Ministry of Health held the highest in-degree values.Spatial analysis, based primarily on self-reported user locations, indicated geographic concentration along the Java-Bali corridor, and temporal analysis revealed recurring peaks in January and June aligned with Indonesia's wet season and dengue outbreak cycles.These findings demonstrate the value of integrating sentiment, network, and spatial dimensions for comprehensive public health communication analysis.
journal: International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems

License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ Examining Dengue-related Information Diffusion on Indonesian Twitter Through Sentiment-based Network Analysis, Spatial Mapping, and Temporal Dynamics Ribka Devina Margaretha1 Wiwik Anggraeni1* 1Department of Information Systems, Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember, Surabaya, Indonesia * Corresponding author’s Email: wiwik@is.its.ac.id Abstract: Dengue fever remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, yet studies integrating sentiment analysis, Social Network Analysis, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on social media remain limited. This study proposes an integrated framework applied to 5,715 dengue-related tweets collected from Indonesian Twitter between January 2021 and December 2025. Sentiment classification using IndoBERT revealed a predominantly neutral discourse (65.23%), with meaningful negative (20.31%) and positive (14.45%) proportions. Sentiment-weighted interaction networks were constructed and analysed, revealing highly fragmented structures with modularity scores exceeding 0.98. Healthcare professionals emerged as the most robustly influential actors by betweenness centrality, with PageRank-based influence conditional on self-loop treatment, while the Ministry of Health held the highest in-degree values. Spatial analysis, based primarily on self-reported user locations, indicated geographic concentration along the Java-Bali corridor, and temporal analysis revealed recurring peaks in January and June aligned with Indonesia's wet season and dengue outbreak cycles. These findings demonstrate the value of integrating sentiment, network, and spatial dimensions for comprehensive public health communication analysis. Keywords: Dengue fever, Sentiment-based network analysis, Spatial analysis, Temporal analysis, Social media. 1. Introduction Dengue fever remains one of the fastest- spreading vector-borne diseases and a major global public health challenge, endemic in more than 100 countries and threatening approximately 3.9 billion people, particularly in Southeast Asia and Latin America [1-3]. In Indonesia, dengue is highly endemic and continues to cause serious health problems, with more than 257,000 reported cases and over 1,400 deaths in 2024 [4]. The increasing spread of dengue, driven by climate change, urbanisation, and population growth, has also heightened public concern regarding outbreaks and prevention efforts [5]. The growing use of social media, particularly Twitter, has created new opportunities to observe public responses and information exchange related to disease outbreaks[6-8]. Through mentions, replies, and reposts, Twitter enables rapid information diffusion across communities, while certain accounts play disproportionately influential roles in shaping discussions [9]. Social Network Analysis (SNA) has therefore been widely applied to identify influential actors and examine information diffusion dynamics within online networks [10, 11]. Beyond interaction patterns, social media discussions also reflect public opinions and emotional responses toward ongoing health issues [12]. Sentiment analysis provides a complementary approach for capturing these perceptions, and incorporating sentiment information into network analysis can deepen understanding of how dengue- related discussions propagate and evolve on social media [13]. Dengue burden and public health responses are not uniformly distributed across Indonesia, with substantial disparities observed across provinces and Received: June 15, 2026. Revised: July 16, 2026. 686 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.35 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ regions due to differences in population density, climate conditions, healthcare accessibility, and vector control capacity [14, 15]. Public perceptions and responses to health information also vary across communities due to cultural and social differences [16]. These regional variations highlight the importance of incorporating spatial information to better understand geographic differences in dengue- related discussions, public sentiment, and information dissemination patterns. Previous studies have applied SNA to identify influential users and examine information diffusion in online discussions, while sentiment analysis has been widely used to understand public perceptions toward health-related issues, and spatial analysis has been employed to reveal geographic variations in dengue transmission and public health responses. However, these approaches are typically investigated in isolation, limiting a comprehensive understanding of how interaction structures, public sentiment, and geographic context collectively shape online discussions. Studies integrating sentiment-weighted social networks with spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on Indonesian Twitter remain particularly limited, highlighting the need for a more integrated analytical framework. To address this gap, this study integrates sentiment analysis, SNA, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related Twitter discussions, constructing sentiment-weighted interaction networks and analysing them alongside geographic and temporal dimensions. The specific contributions of this study are: • Analysis of the spatial distribution of discussions and sentiments across Indonesian cities • Construction of sentiment-based interaction networks capturing both communication structure and public perception • Identification of national-level influential users using PageRank, degree centrality, and betweenness centrality • Identification of regional influential users across multiple Indonesian cities • Analysis of temporal discussion patterns and sentiment dynamics • Visualisation of interaction networks illustrating information diffusion structures. The remainder of this paper is structured as follows. Section 2 reviews related literature. Section 3 describes the data and methodology. Section 4 presents the results and discussion. Section 5 summarises the findings and outlines future directions. 2. Related works 2.1 Social network analysis for information diffusion SNA has been widely applied to investigate information diffusion and interaction patterns in online social networks, modelling users as nodes and interactions as edges to identify influential actors and community structures [17]. Various approaches have been proposed for influencer detection, including the NetDegree centrality measure and the Weighted Correlated Influence (WCI) model combining user activity and network topology [18, 19]. SNA has also been applied to explore community structures and communication dynamics in domain-specific discussions [20]. In health-related contexts, SNA has been used to identify key influencers, dominant topics, and communication structures shaping public awareness [10, 11, 21]. However, most existing health-related SNA studies focus on network topology and influencer identification without incorporating sentiment context or geographic variation. Bonifazi et al. identified influential users in COVID-19 vaccine Twitter discourse through a multilayer network approach, but did not construct sentiment-segmented networks or examine geographic distributions [21]. Durmaz and Hengirmen applied SNA to vaccine- related Twitter discourse in Turkey using in-degree and betweenness centrality, but did not integrate sentiment labels or examine spatial distributions [22]. Pratiwi et al. combined SNA and sentiment analysis for asthma-related Twitter discourse, but did not link findings to geographic distributions or construct sentiment-segmented networks [10]. The absence of sentiment integration and spatial context in these studies limits the depth of understanding achievable in health-related discourse analysis. 2.2 Sentiment analysis in social media discussions Sentiment analysis is widely applied to understand public opinions in social media, with recent studies demonstrating the effectiveness of advanced language models including IndoBERT for Indonesian-language content [23, 24]. Ishfaq et al. and Eliacik and Erdogan have incorporated sentiment into network-based analyses for influential user identification [25, 26]. However, applications combining sentiment and network characteristics in health-related discussions remain limited. Dengue-specific sentiment studies such as Abdul Ghani et al. demonstrate the value of sentiment for disease surveillance but do not Received: June 15, 2026. Revised: July 16, 2026. 687 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.35 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ construct interaction networks or link findings to geographic distributions [27]. Indonesian-language classification studies such as Supriyadi and Makatita and Nabiilah et al. demonstrate strong model performance without connecting findings to network structures or spatial patterns [23, 24]. While Ishfaq et al. and Eliacik and Erdogan incorporate sentiment into network analyses, neither examined dengue- related discourse or linked findings to spatial distributions [25, 26]. No prior study has simultaneously applied sentiment-integrated SNA to dengue-related Indonesian Twitter data, leaving a gap in understanding how emotional responses and interaction structures collectively shape dengue information diffusion. 2.3 Spatial analysis in health-related studies Spatial analysis has gained increasing attention in public health and social media research for understanding geographic variations in behaviour and information dissemination. Lovera and Cardinale demonstrated that geolocation enriches the interpretation of social media discussions [34]. Similarly, Wu et al. highlighted the value of geospatial enrichment for understanding large-scale sentiment behaviour[35]. In health-related contexts, Lin et al. revealed linguistic and geographic disparities in COVID-19 public awareness through social media, while Zhang et al. applied geographical and temporal analysis to health-related tweets to identify spatiotemporal disease discussion patterns at regional level [36, 37]. However, these studies focus on geographic distribution patterns without modelling user interaction networks or identifying regional-level influential users. Lin et al., Zhang et al., Lovera and Cardinale, and Wu et al. all incorporate geolocation into social media analysis, but do not construct interaction networks, identify influential users, or examine how sentiment varies across network communities [z-37]. Studies applying spatial analysis to dengue-related social media discourse, such as Abdul Ghani et al., have similarly focused on geographic mapping without modelling user interaction dynamics or examining sentiment- segmented network structures [27]. The absence of interaction network modelling and sentiment integration limits understanding of how network dynamics and public sentiment collectively shape dengue information diffusion. 2.4 Research gap Despite the established contributions of SNA, sentiment analysis, and spatial analysis individually, existing health-related social media studies address these dimensions in isolation, as demonstrated across Sections 2.1 to 2.3, focusing on network topology without sentiment context [10, 21, 22], applying sentiment classification without network or spatial linkage[23, 27], or examining geographic patterns without modelling interaction dynamics [34-37]. While sentiment analysis and network approaches have each been applied to health-related social media discourse individually, their simultaneous integration with spatial analysis in the specific context of dengue-related Indonesian Twitter data remains unexplored. No prior study has proposed a unified framework simultaneously capturing the structural, emotional, and geographic dimensions of dengue-related information diffusion on Indonesian Twitter. This study addresses that gap by integrating sentiment analysis, SNA, and spatial analysis within a single framework, constructing sentiment- segmented interaction networks to examine how different emotional contexts shape network structure and influencer profiles, mapping discussion distributions and regional influencer patterns across Indonesian cities, and tracing temporal dynamics of both discussion volume and sentiment evolution over a five-year period. This integrated approach offers a more complete understanding of information dissemination patterns, influential users, and public perceptions across different locations and time periods than prior single-method studies have provided. 3. Materials and method 3.1 Dataset Dengue-related tweets were collected from Twitter (X) between January 2021 and December 2025 using the Scweet Python library with three keywords: "dbd" (dengue haemorrhagic fever acronym in Indonesian), "Aedes aegypti" (the dengue-carrying mosquito species), and "demam berdarah dengue" (dengue haemorrhagic fever). Data collection was conducted between 9-14 April 2026. The collected tweets span the period from January 2021 to December 2025, reflecting the full range of historical tweets retrievable through Scweet at the time of collection; Scweet retrieves historical tweets via browser automation rather than the official Twitter/X API, and collection completeness is therefore subject to the platform's search indexing and any rate-limiting constraints encountered during scraping. All tweets included in this study represent observed data retrieved directly through Scweet; no Received: June 15, 2026. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ projected, simulated, or placeholder records are included in the dataset or in any reported analysis. Collection was conducted as a series of discrete scraping sessions per keyword and sub-period, with no session returning a tweet count at or exceeding the configured retrieval limit (500-1,000 tweets, depending on keyword), indicating retrieval without truncation within each queried window. A completeness check was performed by examining the year-by-year distribution of collected tweets to confirm the absence of anomalous gaps or artificially uniform collection patterns; as detailed in Section 4.6.1, tweet volume varied organically across the five-year period, consistent with externally documented dengue activity patterns in Indonesia rather than indicating systematic data loss. Each tweet record contains textual content, publication date, user information, engagement statistics, and interaction attributes including mentions, replies, and reposts. The collected dataset serves as the primary source for all sentiment, network, spatial, and temporal analyses conducted in this study. 3.2 Method This study employs an integrated analytical framework consisting of data preprocessing, sentiment classification, network construction, community detection, spatial analysis, and temporal analysis. Data preprocessing The datasets collected from different periods were combined and filtered to retain only the attributes required for analysis, including tweet identifiers, usernames, tweet content, timestamps, language information, location attributes, and interaction metadata. User mentions and replies were extracted separately to support network construction. Duplicate tweets and records with missing values in essential attributes were removed, and tweet texts were cleaned through lowercasing, URL removal, mention and hashtag removal, number and punctuation removal, and whitespace normalisation. Tweets that became empty after cleaning were discarded, and only Indonesian-language tweets were retained. Examples of tweets before and after preprocessing are shown in Table 1. For spatial analysis, location information was obtained from tweet-level and user profile locations, with the latter used as a fallback when tweet-level location was unavailable. Location texts were normalised and matched against a reference dataset of Indonesian cities, with common aliases and abbreviations standardised to improve matching accuracy. This process successfully mapped 3,327 tweets (58.22%) to 168 Indonesian cities. 3.2.2. Sentiment analysis Sentiment analysis was conducted to identify public opinions expressed in dengue-related Twitter discussions. elements_en.methods: Dengue fever remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, yet studies integrating sentiment analysis, Social Network Analysis, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on social media remain limited.This study proposes an integrated framework applied to 5,715 dengue-related tweets collected from Indonesian Twitter between January 2021 and December 2025.Sentiment classification using IndoBERT revealed a predominantly neutral discourse (65.23%), with meaningful negative (20.31%) and positive (14.45%) proportions.Sentiment-weighted interaction networks were constructed and analysed, revealing highly fragmented structures with modularity scores exceeding 0.98.Healthcare professionals emerged as the most robustly influential actors by betweenness centrality, with PageRank-based influence conditional on self-loop treatment, while the Ministry of Health held the highest in-degree values.Spatial analysis, based primarily on self-reported user locations, indicated geographic concentration along the Java-Bali corridor, and temporal analysis revealed recurring peaks in January and June aligned with Indonesia's wet season and dengue outbreak cycles.These findings demonstrate the value of integrating sentiment, network, and spatial dimensions for comprehensive public health communication analysis.

elements_zh.methods: 登革热 仍然是印度尼西亚的一项重大公共卫生挑战,但整合情感分析、社交网络分析和空间分析来检查社交媒体上登革热相关信息传播的研究仍然有限。这项研究提出了一个综合框架,应用于 2021 年 1 月至 2025 年 12 月期间从印度尼西亚 Twitter 收集的 5,715 条登革热相关推文。使用 IndoBERT 进行的情感分类显示,主要是中性话语 (65.23%),有意义的负面言论(20.31%) 和正 (14.45%) 比例。构建和建立了情感加权交互网络,揭示了高度碎片化的结构,模块化得分超过 0.98。医疗保健专业人员通过介数中心性成为最具影响力的参与者,基于 PageRank 的影响力以自循环 治疗 为条件,而卫生部拥有最高的入度值。空间分析,主要基于用户自我报告位置、表明爪哇-巴厘岛走廊沿线的地理集中度以及时间分析显示 1 月和 6 月反复出现的高峰与印度尼西亚的雨季和登革热 暴发 周期一致。这些发现证明了整合情绪、网络和空间维度对于全面公共卫生传播分析的价值。

title_zh: 通过基于情感的网络分析、空间映射和时间动态检查印度尼西亚 Twitter 上与登革热相关的信息传播
source_body_en: Dengue fever remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, yet studies integrating sentiment analysis, Social Network Analysis, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on social media remain limited.This study proposes an integrated framework applied to 5,715 dengue-related tweets collected from Indonesian Twitter between January 2021 and December 2025.Sentiment classification using IndoBERT revealed a predominantly neutral discourse (65.23%), with meaningful negative (20.31%) and positive (14.45%) proportions.Sentiment-weighted interaction networks were constructed and analysed, revealing highly fragmented structures with modularity scores exceeding 0.98.Healthcare professionals emerged as the most robustly influential actors by betweenness centrality, with PageRank-based influence conditional on self-loop treatment, while the Ministry of Health held the highest in-degree values.Spatial analysis, based primarily on self-reported user locations, indicated geographic concentration along the Java-Bali corridor, and temporal analysis revealed recurring peaks in January and June aligned with Indonesia's wet season and dengue outbreak cycles.These findings demonstrate the value of integrating sentiment, network, and spatial dimensions for comprehensive public health communication analysis.
abstract_zh: 登革热 仍然是印度尼西亚的一项重大公共卫生挑战,但整合情感分析、社交网络分析和空间分析来检查社交媒体上登革热相关信息传播的研究仍然有限。这项研究提出了一个综合框架,应用于 2021 年 1 月至 2025 年 12 月期间从印度尼西亚 Twitter 收集的 5,715 条登革热相关推文。使用 IndoBERT 进行的情感分类显示,主要是中性话语 (65.23%),有意义的负面言论(20.31%) 和正 (14.45%) 比例。构建和建立了情感加权交互网络,揭示了高度碎片化的结构,模块化得分超过 0.98。医疗保健专业人员通过介数中心性成为最具影响力的参与者,基于 PageRank 的影响力以自循环 治疗 为条件,而卫生部拥有最高的入度值。空间分析,主要基于用户自我报告位置、表明爪哇-巴厘岛走廊沿线的地理集中度以及时间分析显示 1 月和 6 月反复出现的高峰与印度尼西亚的雨季和登革热 暴发 周期一致。这些发现证明了整合情绪、网络和空间维度对于全面公共卫生传播分析的价值。

full_text: L’ESSENTIEL - Le moustique-tigre pourrait conquérir jusqu’à 96 % de la France hexagonale d’ici à 2085. - Dengue mais aussi Zika et chikungunya pourraient ainsi émerger sur presque tout l’Hexagone, montre une nouvelle étude - Les zones rurales et périurbaines seront les plus à risque. Le moustique-tigre (Aedes albopictus) est arrivé accidentellement en France en 2004. Mais d’ici à 2085, on pourra le trouver dans tout l’Hexagone à l’exception des zones de haute montagne, et peut-être de certaines régions intérieures du nord. En conséquence, montre notre nouvelle étude, la dengue et les virus Zika et chikungunya transmis par cet insecte pourraient également se répandre dans toutes ces zones colonisées, hormis peut-être la côte de la Manche. L’expansion de ces maladies est la conséquence directe du changement climatique, qui modifie la répartition géographique de différentes espèces, principalement par le biais de l’augmentation des températures, et continuera à le faire pendant encore plusieurs décennies. Lorsque les températures de l’Hexagone se rapprochent de celles des régions tropicales, où le moustique-tigre a évolué pendant des milliers d’années, cet insecte se reproduit et se développe plus rapidement, vit plus longtemps et pique plus souvent. Comprendre ce changement est primordial pour prévenir le risque majeur qu’il représente pour la santé publique. C’est ce que nous avons voulu faire à travers notre nouvelle étude. Comment ces prévisions ont-elles été réalisées ? Pour cela, nous avons utilisé des modèles mathématiques qui permettent d’estimer la population de moustiques à un endroit donné à un moment précis. Ces modèles nous permettent de simuler l’évolution de ces peuplements de moustiques en utilisant des séries de projections météorologiques nous permettant de regrouper des paramètres comme la température, les précipitations, l’abondance des sites de reproduction... Pour cette étude, nous avons utilisé des projections du GIEC pour les soixante prochaines années, qui varient en fonction des politiques climatiques futures : nous avons distingué un scénario « haute pression » (+ 3 °C et sur la période 2066-2085 par rapport à la période 1986-2005) et un scénario « moyenne pression » (+ 1,8 °C). Ces deux trajectoires se traduisent directement sur l’expansion du moustique-tigre : dans le premier cas, entre 89 et 96 % du territoire deviendrait favorable à son implantation, dans le deuxième, cette expansion baisse à 72 %. Ce que ces travaux nous permettent de comprendre Si cette étude n’est pas la première à s’intéresser à l’impact du changement climatique sur les moustiques-tigres, elle propose cependant des prévisions d’une précision inédite pour le territoire hexagonal. Elle nous permet ainsi de caractériser le risque épidémiologique en observant les différences de risque à différentes latitudes ainsi qu’entre les zones urbaines et périurbaines. Bien que les villes hébergent davantage de moustiques, nos simulations montrent ainsi que les zones rurales et périurbaines seront plus vulnérables à la transmission que les grandes villes, car chaque moustique y pique un plus petit nombre de personnes de façon répétée, augmentant ainsi le potentiel de propagation. Nous sommes également parmi les premiers à avoir étudié la possibilité de moustiques actifs toute l’année du fait d’hivers doux, qui leur permettraient de ne plus avoir besoin d’hiberner. Comment poursuivre ces recherches ? La France hexagonale va donc devoir composer avec le moustique-tigre. Pour minimiser les risques de transmission de maladie, des études à une échelle encore plus fines pourraient être d’une grande aide, afin de documenter l’interaction entre le moustique-tigre et l’humain en fonction de conditions locales telles que la végétalisation des villes, la gestion de l’eau, les pratiques de lutte contre les vecteurs. En comparant toutes ces données, nous pourrions ainsi identifier les pratiques qui minimisent les risques. Parallèlement, il faut étudier la mise en œuvre opérationnelle des modèles, afin de mettre au point un outil que chaque citoyen pourrait consulter. À Montpellier (Hérault), la communauté des modélisateurs travaille en étroite collaboration avec les collectivités, les responsables de la santé publique et les agences de lutte contre les vecteurs afin de produire un outil adapté. Bientôt, nous pourrons ainsi, au-delà des prévisions météorologiques, proposer au public une « météo des moustiques ». Tout savoir en trois minutes sur des résultats récents de recherches, commentés et contextualisés par les chercheuses et les chercheurs qui ont menées ces dernières, c’est le principe de nos « Research Briefs ». Un format à retrouver ici.

full_text: AbstractRNA virus infections are shaped by the interplay among viral replication, innate immune sensing, and host metabolism, which together determine the magnitude, duration, and quality of antiviral responses. The tryptophan–kynurenine (Trp–Kyn) pathway has emerged as an important immunometabolic axis linking interferon-driven inflammation, amino acid availability, immune-cell function, tissue homeostasis, and viral persistence. This review examines the roles of indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1), IDO2, tryptophan 2,3-dioxygenase (TDO), Trp depletion, general control nonderepressible 2 (GCN2) signaling, mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1), Kyn-derived metabolites, and aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) activation in host responses to RNA virus infection. We integrate genetic, pharmacological, cellular, animal, and clinical evidence across positive-sense and negative-sense single-stranded RNA viruses, double-stranded RNA viruses, and reverse-transcribing RNA viruses, including SARS-CoV-2, dengue virus, Zika virus, hepatitis C virus, influenza A virus, respiratory syncytial virus, rotavirus, reovirus, HIV-1, and SIV. Across these systems, the Trp–Kyn–AhR axis can influence interferon responses, viral replication, immune-cell function, tissue injury, and disease outcome. EMCV myocarditis provides causal proof of principle, whereas other RNA-virus models provide complementary functional and clinical evidence. Importantly, pathway activation does not confer a uniform antiviral or pathogenic phenotype; its biological consequences depend on viral class, tissue tropism, viral burden, inflammatory intensity, cell type, and disease stage. On this basis, we propose a time-phase model in which early or excessive IDO1–Kyn–AhR signaling may impair type I interferon responses, NK-cell function, CD8+ T-cell expansion, and viral clearance, whereas appropriately regulated activation during later inflammatory or resolution phases may limit immunopathology, support epithelial repair, and preserve tissue homeostasis. Persistent or dysregulated activation may instead contribute to exhaustion-like immune states, chronic inflammation, neuroimmune dysfunction, and post-acute viral sequelae. Finally, we discuss phase-adapted therapeutic strategies, including IDO1 inhibition, AhR agonism or antagonism, KMO-directed modulation, Trp-based entry inhibitors, and biomarker-guided combination approaches. Together, these findings position the Trp–Kyn–AhR axis as a dynamic, context-dependent target for precision host-directed antiviral immunometabolism.Keywords: antiviral immunity, aryl hydrocarbon receptor, host-directed antiviral therapy, IDO1, immunometabolism, RNA viruses, tissue repair, tryptophan-kynurenine pathway 6.Conclusions and future perspectivesThe Trp–Kyn–AhR axis is an important immunometabolic regulator of RNA virus infection. Causal evidence from EMCV and LP-BM5, in vivo IAV studies, functional perturbation of IDO1, KMO, or AhR, and human association studies indicate that this pathway can influence viral burden, interferon responses, immune-cell function, tissue injury, and survival. Because these outcomes may diverge across models, biological relevance should not be inferred from a uniform phenotype across infections. Accordingly, increased IDO1 expression or elevated Kyn/Trp ratios should be interpreted as evidence of pathway engagement rather than as direct markers of antiviral activity or pathogenicity. Mechanistic interpretation requires integration with viral kinetics, interferon responses, immune-cell function, tissue-injury markers, and compartment-specific metabolite measurements (25, 26, 90).Our proposed time-phase model provides a testable framework in which pathway function is evaluated across defined stages and tissues rather than inferred retrospectively from disease severity. It predicts that the same node may impair antiviral pressure before viral clearance yet promote disease tolerance, barrier integrity, or tissue repair when immunopathology predominates (27, 28).Therapeutic translation therefore depends on when, where, and in whom the pathway is targeted. IDO1 inhibitors, KMO modulators, or AhR antagonists should be prioritized only when genetic and pharmacological evidence converge and when target engagement, PK/PD, virological efficacy, and tissue-level effects are demonstrated in relevant models.Future studies should focus on underexplored RNA viruses and combine longitudinal metabolomics with viral load, interferon signaling, spatial or cell-resolved profiling, and genetic or pharmacological rescue experiments. Such approaches will help distinguish shared, therapeutically actionable dependencies from virus-, tissue-, or phase-specific effects (15, 31). Post-acute disease also warrants dedicated investigation, as persistent IDO2/AhR activity, altered NAD metabolism, and neuroactive Kyn metabolites may reflect unresolved inflammation, compensatory responses, or causal pathology that can only be distinguished through longitudinal perturbation studies.Overall, the Trp–Kyn–AhR axis is biologically well supported but therapeutically immature. Its immediate value lies in converting current mechanistic gaps into testable hypotheses, using EMCV as causal proof of principle while preserving virus- and context-specific biology to guide the development of antiviral immunometabolic strategies. 1.IntroductionRNA viruses are among the most active categories of human diseases, characterized by their rapid replication, substantial genetic diversity, and robust ability to adapt to immunological and therapeutic challenges. A primary factor influencing this plasticity is the restricted proofreading ability of numerous viral RNA-dependent polymerases, which promotes the ongoing production of mutant spectra during replication. The combination of rapid replication cycles and substantial viral population sizes allows RNA viruses to navigate adaptive landscapes, promoting immune evasion, antiviral resistance, host switching, and prolonged persistence (1, 2). These characteristics are fundamental to the biology of clinically significant RNA viruses, such as influenza A virus (IAV), dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), coronaviruses, hepatitis C virus (HCV), and human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1), all of which exemplify how viral evolution and host immune pressure influence infection outcomes (3–5).While RNA virus infections have historically been examined in relation to innate and adaptive immunity, it is now clear that the metabolic condition of both infected cells and immune populations significantly impacts antiviral defense. Immunometabolism has emerged as a conceptual framework that elucidates how metabolic pathways regulate immune cell activation, differentiation, effector functions, and exhaustion. Metabolic changes actively influence the extent and quality of antiviral responses, rather than only serving as passive consequences of inflammation (6, 7). During infection, immune cells undergo significant metabolic reprogramming to support cytokine synthesis, clonal proliferation, antigen presentation, and cytotoxic function. Activated lymphocytes and inflammatory macrophages frequently enhance aerobic glycolysis to rapidly produce ATP and biosynthetic precursors, whereas resting or regulatory cells predominantly rely on oxidative phosphorylation and fatty acid metabolism (8–10).These alterations may promote viral replication while concurrently enhancing inflammatory pathways via mechanisms such as reactive oxygen species generation and nuclear factor kappa B (NFκB) activation (11, 12). The metabolic response to infection can either facilitate antiviral immunity or foster an environment conducive to viral persistence and immunological dysfunction, contingent upon timing, tissue context, and the severity of inflammation (13, 14). In this context, amino acid metabolism has become particularly significant within this framework, as amino acids function not only as substrates for protein synthesis but also as immunological signals that modulate cell proliferation, stress responses, and inflammatory tone (6, 15).Tryptophan (Trp) exemplifies this principle prominently. Trp, an essential amino acid, is required for protein synthesis and serves as a precursor for several bioactive pathways involved in immunological control, brain function, redox balance, and tissue homeostasis. Trp metabolism is primarily distributed among three interconnected pathways: the serotonin pathway, which facilitates the production of serotonin and melatonin; the indole pathway, which produces various AhR ligands derived from microbiota and the host; and the kynurenine (Kyn) pathway, which is responsible for the majority of systemic Trp degradation and yields metabolites with immunoregulatory and metabolic functions, including Kyn, kynurenic acid, quinolinic acid, and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide precursors (16–18).The Kyn pathway has gained significance in viral immunology due to its high induction by inflammatory and interferon-mediated signals. The route commences with Trp-catabolizing enzymes, namely indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1), indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 2 (IDO2), and tryptophan 2,3-dioxygenase (TDO2). IDO1 is the most inducible enzyme in inflammatory tissues. It is frequently elevated in response to interferon-gamma (IFN-γ), type I interferons, Toll-like receptor signaling, interleukin-1, and various inflammatory mediators produced during infection (19, 20). Upon activation, IDO1 diverts Trp metabolism towards Kyn synthesis, thereby reducing local Trp availability and elevating levels of metabolites that can alter immunological responses (15, 21).Encephalomyocarditis virus (EMCV) myocarditis provides strong proof of principle for the role of the Kyn pathway in RNA virus infection. In Ido1−/− mice and in wild-type mice treated with 1-methyl-D, L-tryptophan, disruption of IDO1 activity enhanced type I interferon responses, reduced the cardiac viral burden, and improved survival. Administration of Kyn-pathway metabolites reversed this protection. Bone marrow chimera experiments supported a contribution from hematopoietic cells, and Kmo deficiency independently reduced mortality. Together, these findings demonstrate that direct perturbation of the pathway can modify both RNA virus control and disease outcome (22, 23).Beyond EMCV, complementary evidence has emerged from genetic and pharmacological studies in IAV and LP-BM5; functional perturbation of IDO1, KMO, or AhR in ZIKV, coronaviruses, and CSFV; cell-based studies in RSV and HCV; and clinical metabolomic or immunological associations in COVID-19, DENV, influenza, and HIV/SIV. Although these models do not produce an identical phenotype, collectively they indicate that distinct nodes of the Trp-Kyn-AhR axis can influence viral replication, interferon responses, immune-cell function, and tissue injury (19, 24–28).A central unresolved question is therefore not simply whether the pathway participates in antiviral immunity, but when and under which biological conditions its activity is protective or detrimental. Depending on the infection stage and tissue context, pathway activation may constrain antiviral immune pressure, limit immunopathology, or contribute to tissue adaptation and repair. Distinguishing among these functions is particularly important for defining the timing and tissue specificity of therapeutic interventions targeting IDO1, KMO, or AhR (29–33).Accordingly, this review examines the Kyn pathway as a dynamic and temporally regulated immunometabolic axis during RNA virus infection. We first outline the molecular mechanisms through which interferon signaling, Trp depletion, GCN2 activation, and Kyn-mediated AhR signaling shape antiviral immunity. We then critically examine evidence across major RNA virus infections, including SARS-CoV-2, IAV, DENV, ZIKV, RSV, HCV, and HIV, identifying not only the principal mechanistic and translational findings but also the major gaps in knowledge that remain across these infections. These unresolved questions are discussed as opportunities for future research, particularly for defining when and how modulation of the Trp-Kyn-AhR axis could be exploited for antiviral development or as a host-directed therapeutic strategy. Finally, we propose a therapeutic-window model in which the biological consequences of targeting this axis depend on infection timing, viral burden, inflammatory severity, and tissue-specific immune regulation. The overarching immunometabolic framework, current knowledge gaps, and therapeutic opportunities discussed throughout this review are summarized in Figure 1.Figure 1Overview of the Trp–Kyn–AhR immunometabolic axis during RNA virus infection. (1) Viral RNA recognition by pattern-recognition receptors (PRRs), including RIG-I, MDA5, and TLRs, triggers inflammatory cytokines and interferons that activate immunometabolic responses in epithelial cells, dendritic cells, macrophages, and other immune cells. (2) Tryptophan (Trp) is catabolized by the rate-limiting enzymes IDO1, IDO2, and TDO, yielding kynurenine (Kyn) and downstream metabolites such as kynurenic acid (KYNA), 3-hydroxykynurenine (3-HK), and quinolinic acid (QUIN). Trp depletion and Kyn accumulation constitute the central metabolic switch of the pathway. (3) Kyn and related metabolites activate the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR), promoting AhR–ARNT nuclear translocation and the transcription of immune-regulatory genes. Simultaneously, Trp depletion activates GCN2 and suppresses mTORC1 signaling, thereby coordinating nutrient sensing, translational control, and cellular stress adaptation. (4) Integration of these signaling pathways regulates immune-cell differentiation and function. Balanced activation promotes controlled antiviral immunity and tissue homeostasis, whereas sustained activation promotes regulatory immune programs, impairs effector-cell activity, promotes immune tolerance, and favors viral persistence.Infographic outlining the sequence of viral infection effects: Panel one shows viral recognition and cytokine signaling in sensing cells by RNA virus types. Panel two illustrates tryptophan metabolism through the kynurenine pathway. Panel three details AhR activation by kynurenine and derived ligands, with downstream gene programs and nutrient-sensing pathway activation. Panel four contrasts protective versus harmful immunological outcomes, with adaptive responses shown at the top and prolonged harmful effects, such as immune suppression and tissue damage, shown at the bottom. 2.Immunometabolic regulation of the tryptophan-kynurenine pathwayViewing the Kyn pathway as a time-dependent immunometabolic switch raises a central mechanistic question: how does Trp metabolism translate inflammatory sensing into altered antiviral immunity? During RNA virus infection, pattern-recognition receptors, interferons, inflammatory cytokines, nutrient-sensing pathways, and tissue-repair programs act in concert to shape host responses (6, 15). Within this network, the Trp-Kyn pathway links inflammatory signaling to metabolic and transcriptional regulation of innate and adaptive immunity (21) through three interconnected processes: cytokine-driven IDO1 induction, nutrient-stress signaling triggered by Trp depletion, and receptor-mediated immune regulation by Kyn metabolites. The resulting effects vary according to cell type, tissue, infection stage, and the virological or pathological endpoint examined (34–36).2.1.Interferon-driven activation of IDO1IDO1 catalyzes the first and rate-limiting step of extrahepatic Trp degradation through the Kyn pathway (37, 38), linking antiviral cytokine signaling to metabolic restriction and immune-cell reprogramming (15, 21). Among its inflammatory inducers, IFN-γ is the most potent physiological regulator. Produced mainly by activated T lymphocytes and NK cells, IFN-γ signals through IFNGR1/IFNGR2 to activate the JAK1/JAK2-STAT1 pathway. Phosphorylated STAT1 translocates to the nucleus and, together with IRF1, promotes transcriptional programs involved in antimicrobial defense, antigen presentation, immune regulation, and IDO1 expression (39, 40).The IFN-γ-JAK-STAT1-IRF1 axis induces IDO1 particularly in macrophages and dendritic cells, although epithelial, endothelial, microglial, and other tissue-resident cells can also express IDO1 under inflammatory conditions, enabling local regulation at sites of viral replication and tissue injury (38, 40). Once induced, IDO1 simultaneously reduces local Trp availability and increases Kyn and other bioactive metabolites, thereby altering the metabolic and signaling environment of immune cells (37, 38). These effects are especially relevant to activated lymphocytes, which require adequate amino-acid availability for clonal expansion, cytokine production, and cytotoxic function (21, 41).The consequences of IDO1 activation during viral infection are context- and time-dependent. Early activity may limit excessive inflammation and tissue damage, whereas sustained activation can promote an immunoregulatory environment associated with impaired CD8+ T-cell and NK-cell function, regulatory T-cell expansion, and ineffective persistent inflammation (42, 43). This duality is particularly evident in SARS-CoV-2 infection, in which enhanced Trp catabolism and Kyn-pathway activity have been associated with systemic inflammation and disease severity (44, 45).Beyond Trp catabolism, IDO1 can also exert non-catalytic signaling functions that reinforce tolerogenic programs (46).
